steps: Who depends on bees? Mustard flowers need bees to carry pollen
Fewer bees means fewer flowers get pollinated
Fewer pollinated flowers means fewer pods and seeds
Fewer seeds means less mustard oil and less income for farmers
Conclusion: losing one species affects plants and people
fadedVersion: Who depends on bees? Mustard flowers need bees to carry ___
Fewer bees means fewer flowers get ___
Fewer pollinated flowers means fewer ___
Fewer seeds means less ___ and less income
Conclusion: losing one species affects ___ and people

skills.title: Name the nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals) plus dietary fibre and water
Match each nutrient to its main role in the body
Identify the main nutrients in everyday Indian foods

expectations: Food contains nutrients: carbohydrates and fats mainly give energy; proteins help the body grow and repair itself; vitamins and minerals protect us and keep the body working well.
Dietary fibre (roughage) helps digestion and the passing out of waste; water helps digest food, carry substances around the body and remove waste.

Carbohydrates: rice, wheat, millets, potato. Proteins: dal, rajma, chana, milk, paneer, eggs, fish. Fats: ghee, oil, butter, nuts. Vitamins and minerals: fruits, vegetables, milk. Fibre: whole grains, vegetables, fruits.
Fats give about twice as much energy as the same amount of carbohydrate.
Nutritious food need not be costly: local seasonal foods like dal, chana, amla, guava, green leafy vegetables and millets are rich in nutrients.

misconceptions.belief: Only costly foods are nutritious.
signs: Says packaged or imported foods are 'healthier' than dal or amla
Ranks foods by price
Dismisses home food as ordinary

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which breakfast gives a good mix of nutrients?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kaunsa naashta poshak tatvon ka achha mel deta hai?

options.text: Poha with peanuts and vegetables, a glass of milk and a banana
An expensive chocolate pastry and a cold drink
Just one bowl of plain rice

remediation.representation: Price tag vs nutrient card for amla, guava, dal and a packaged snack side by side
remediation.moveShape: Child guesses which is most nutritious from the price, then flips the nutrient cards and explains the surprise

misconceptions.belief: All fats are bad and should be avoided completely.
signs: Says 'never eat ghee or oil'
Thinks the body never needs fat

diagnostic.prompt_en: What should we do about fats like ghee and oil?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ghee aur tel jaise fats ke saath kya karna chahiye?

options.text: Never eat any fat at all
Eat a small amount; fats give energy and help the body use some vitamins
Eat as much as we like because they give energy

remediation.representation: Thali plate with a small marked portion for fat
remediation.moveShape: Contrast 'none', 'a little' and 'a lot'; child says what goes wrong in the first and last

misconceptions.belief: Protein comes only from meat and eggs.
signs: Says vegetarians cannot get protein
Doesn't count dal, milk or paneer as protein foods

diagnostic.prompt_en: Meera is vegetarian. Where can she get protein?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Meera vegetarian hai. Use protein kahan se milega?

options.text: Nowhere; protein comes only from meat and eggs
Dal, rajma, chana, milk, paneer, soybean and nuts
Only from sugar and rice

remediation.representation: Vegetarian protein plate: dal, rajma, paneer, curd, peanuts
remediation.moveShape: Child builds a full-protein vegetarian day from the cards, then compares it with a non-vegetarian one

items.prompt_en: Name the five main nutrients in food, and two other things food gives that our body needs.
items.prompt_hi: Khaane ke paanch mukhya poshak tatva batao, aur do aur cheezein jo khaane se milti hain aur shareer ko chahiye.
items.answer: Carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins and minerals; plus dietary fibre (roughage) and water.
hints: Ask what roti, dal and ghee each give
Point to fruits and vegetables for the protective ones
Prompt: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, ___ and ___
Assert: five nutrients plus fibre and water

verified.solverAnswer: Carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals; plus water and roughage (fibre).

items.prompt_en: Which nutrient helps a child grow and repairs a cut or wound?
items.prompt_hi: Kaunsa poshak tatva bachche ko badhne mein aur chot ya ghaav bharne mein madad karta hai?
items.answer: Proteins.
hints: Ask what the body needs to build new skin
Point to dal and milk
Prompt: body-building nutrients are ___
Assert: proteins grow and repair the body

verified.solverAnswer: Protein.

items.prompt_en: Sort these foods by the main nutrient they give: rice, dal, ghee, guava, roti.
items.prompt_hi: In khaanon ko unke mukhya poshak tatva ke hisaab se baanto: chawal, dal, ghee, amrood, roti.
items.answer: Rice: carbohydrate. Dal: protein. Ghee: fat. Guava: vitamins (especially vitamin C) and fibre. Roti: carbohydrate (and fibre if whole wheat).
hints: Ask which foods give quick energy
Point to dal as the body-builder
Prompt: ghee is a ___ and guava gives ___
Assert: rice and roti carbs, dal protein, ghee fat, guava vitamins

verified.solverAnswer: Rice carbohydrate; dal protein; ghee fat; guava vitamins (C); roti carbohydrate.

items.prompt_en: Predict: which has more protein, a bowl of cooked moong dal or a bowl of plain cooked rice of the same size?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: same size ki katori mein, pakki moong dal mein zyada protein hai ya saade pake chawal mein?
items.answer: The moong dal; pulses are rich in protein, while rice is mainly carbohydrate.
hints: Ask what dal is mostly known for
Point to rice as an energy food
Prompt: pulses are rich in ___
Assert: moong dal has more protein

verified.solverAnswer: Dal has more protein.

items.prompt_en: Predict: which gives far more vitamin C, one amla from the local market or one imported packaged apple?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: local bazaar ka ek amla ya ek imported packed seb, kisme kahin zyada vitamin C hai?
items.answer: The amla; it is one of the richest sources of vitamin C, much richer than an apple, and it is cheap and local.
hints: Ask how amla tastes and what sour fruits often have
Point to the price of each
Prompt: the cheap local ___ has more vitamin C
Assert: amla wins; costly doesn't mean more nutritious

verified.solverAnswer: Amla, far more vitamin C.

items.prompt_en: You said dal gives protein. Why does a growing child need protein every day?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne kaha dal se protein milta hai. Badhte bachche ko roz protein kyon chahiye?
items.answer: Proteins are body-building nutrients: the body uses them to make and repair muscles, skin, blood and other parts, and a child's body is growing every day.
hints: Ask what is getting bigger in a child each year
Point to repair after a cut
Prompt: protein is used to ___ and ___ body parts
Assert: protein builds and repairs a growing body

verified.solverAnswer: Protein builds new body parts and repairs; growing body needs it daily.

items.prompt_en: Ghee and sugar both give energy. How are they different as nutrients?
items.prompt_hi: Ghee aur cheeni dono energy dete hain. Poshak tatva ke roop mein dono alag kaise hain?
items.answer: Ghee is a fat and sugar is a carbohydrate; fats give about twice as much energy per gram, and fats also help the body use some vitamins.
hints: Ask which group each belongs to
Point to how much energy a spoon of each gives
Prompt: ghee is a ___ and sugar is a ___
Assert: ghee fat, sugar carbohydrate; fat gives about twice the energy

verified.solverAnswer: Ghee is fat (more concentrated energy, 2x+ per gram, helps vitamins); sugar is a simple carbohydrate giving quick energy.

items.prompt_en: Think of your school mid-day meal, such as khichdi with vegetables. Which nutrients does it give?
items.prompt_hi: Apne school ke mid-day meal ke baare mein socho, jaise sabzi wali khichdi. Isse kaun-kaun se poshak tatva milte hain?
items.answer: Rice gives carbohydrates; dal gives protein; vegetables give vitamins, minerals and fibre; oil or ghee gives fat; and it contains water.
hints: Ask them to list what is inside khichdi
Point to each ingredient one at a time
Prompt: rice → ___, dal → ___, vegetables → ___
Assert: it covers carbohydrates, protein, fat, vitamins, minerals and fibre

verified.solverAnswer: Khichdi: carbohydrate (rice), protein (dal), vitamins/minerals/fibre (vegetables), a bit of fat.

items.prompt_en: A cricket coach plans meals for players during a tournament. Why should the plan include more than just energy foods?
items.prompt_hi: Ek cricket coach tournament ke dauraan khiladiyon ka khaana plan karta hai. Plan mein sirf energy waale khaane se zyada kyon hona chahiye?
items.answer: Players need carbohydrates and fats for energy, proteins to repair and build muscles, vitamins and minerals to stay healthy and recover, water to replace sweat, and fibre for digestion.
hints: Ask what happens to muscles after a long match
Point to sweat lost in the sun
Prompt: energy from carbs, repair from ___, health from ___
Assert: a full plan has every nutrient, fibre and water

verified.solverAnswer: Players need protein for muscle repair, vitamins and minerals, water, not only energy.

items.prompt_en: Draw your thali as a circle and colour each part by what it mainly does: energy food, body-building food or protective food. Describe your thali to me.
items.prompt_hi: Apni thali ko ek circle mein banao aur har hisse ko rang do ki woh mainly kya karta hai: energy, body-building ya protective. Phir mujhe apni thali batao.
items.answer: For example: roti or rice = energy (carbohydrates); dal or curd = body-building (protein); sabzi, salad or fruit = protective (vitamins, minerals, fibre); a little ghee = energy (fat).
hints: Invite them to start with the biggest part of the thali
Point to the dal katori
Prompt: roti is ___ food, dal is ___ food, sabzi is ___ food
Assert: grains energy, dal protein, vegetables protective

verified.solverAnswer: Energy: roti/rice; body building: dal/paneer; protective: vegetables/fruit.

items.prompt_en: Golu says: 'Vegetarians can't get protein, because protein is only in meat and eggs.' Correct him.
items.prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Vegetarian logon ko protein nahi milta, kyonki protein sirf meat aur ande mein hota hai.' Use sahi karo.
items.answer: Plant foods like dal, rajma, chana, soybean and peanuts, and dairy foods like milk, paneer and curd, all give protein.
hints: Ask what is in a bowl of rajma
Point to milk and paneer
Prompt: dal, rajma and paneer all give ___
Assert: many vegetarian foods are rich in protein

verified.solverAnswer: Wrong: dal, pulses, milk, paneer, soy, nuts give protein.

items.prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin what the different nutrients in food do, using foods from your kitchen.
items.prompt_hi: Apne chhote cousin ko samjhao ki khaane ke alag-alag poshak tatva kya karte hain, apne kitchen ke khaane ke example se.
items.answer: Key ideas: carbohydrates (roti, rice) and fats (ghee, oil) give energy; proteins (dal, milk) build and repair the body; vitamins and minerals (fruits, vegetables) protect us; fibre helps digestion; water is needed for everything.
hints: Invite them to pick one food for each nutrient
Point to the job each one does
Prompt: roti gives ___, dal ___, fruit ___
Assert: energy, body-building, protection, plus fibre and water

verified.solverAnswer: Carbs/fats give energy, proteins build/repair, vitamins and minerals protect, fibre aids digestion, water.

items.prompt_en: From last time: what is roughage, and why do we need it?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: roughage kya hai, aur hume iski zaroorat kyon hai?
items.answer: Roughage is dietary fibre, the part of plant food we cannot digest; it helps food move through the gut and prevents constipation.
hints: Ask what part of fruits and vegetables we don't digest
Point to its job in the stomach and gut
Prompt: roughage is another name for ___
Assert: dietary fibre; it keeps digestion moving

verified.solverAnswer: Roughage is fibre in plant foods; not digested, helps bowel movement/avoid constipation.

workedExample.problem: Find the nutrients in a plate of rajma-chawal with salad.
steps: List each food: rajma, rice, salad (cucumber, tomato, onion) and the oil used in cooking
Rice gives carbohydrates for energy
Rajma gives proteins for body-building, and fibre
Salad gives vitamins, minerals and fibre; the oil gives fat
Conclusion: this plate gives carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals and fibre
fadedVersion: List each food: rajma, rice, salad and the ___ used in cooking
Rice gives ___ for energy
Rajma gives ___ for body-building
Salad gives vitamins, minerals and ___; the oil gives ___
Conclusion: this plate gives all the main ___

skills.title: Describe the starch test and its result (dilute iodine turns blue-black)
Describe the paper test for fat and the result of the teacher-run protein test (violet)
Interpret test results and recognise that one food can contain several nutrients

expectations: Starch test: a few drops of dilute iodine solution turn blue-black where starch is present (potato, rice, roti).
Fat test: rubbing a food on paper leaves an oily, translucent patch that does not dry away if fat is present (groundnut, coconut); a water patch dries and disappears.
Protein test (done only with the teacher): the food is mixed with water and drops of copper sulphate and sodium hydroxide solutions; a violet colour shows protein (egg white, milk, moong dal paste).
Iodine shows starch, not every carbohydrate: sugar does not turn blue-black.
One food can contain several nutrients (groundnut has fat and protein; milk has protein and fat).
Food used in tests is never eaten, and chemicals are handled only with a teacher.

misconceptions.belief: A food has only one nutrient.
signs: Says groundnut is 'only fat'
Stops after one positive test
Is surprised that milk shows protein and fat

diagnostic.prompt_en: Groundnut left an oily patch on paper. In the lab, groundnut paste also turned violet in the protein test. What does this show?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Moongphali ne kaagaz pe tel ka daag chhoda. Lab mein moongphali ka paste protein test mein bhi baingani ho gaya. Isse kya pata chalta hai?

options.text: The test went wrong, because a food can have only one nutrient
Groundnuts contain both fat and protein
The paper made the protein

remediation.representation: Result grid: foods down the side, starch, fat and protein across, ticks in several columns per food
remediation.moveShape: Fill the grid together for groundnut and milk; child notices more than one tick per row

misconceptions.belief: The iodine test shows any carbohydrate, including sugar.
signs: Predicts sugar solution will turn blue-black
Says 'sugar is a carbohydrate so it must turn blue-black'

diagnostic.prompt_en: The teacher puts iodine on sugar solution and on rice water. Which turns blue-black?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Teacher cheeni ke ghol aur chawal ke maand pe iodine daalti hain. Kaunsa neela-kaala hoga?

options.text: Both, because both are carbohydrates
Only the rice water, because iodine shows starch, not sugar
Neither of them

remediation.representation: Carbohydrate family tree: starch and sugar as two branches, iodine pointing only at starch
remediation.moveShape: Show the two branches, run the predict-reveal, then ask what the test really detects

misconceptions.belief: Any wet patch on paper means the food has fat.
signs: Says tomato has fat because the paper got wet
Decides before the paper dries

diagnostic.prompt_en: A slice of tomato rubbed on paper makes a wet patch. What should you do before deciding?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Tamatar ka tukda kaagaz pe ragadne se geela daag bana. Decide karne se pehle kya karna chahiye?

options.text: Decide right away that it has fat
Let the paper dry; if the patch disappears, it was water, not fat
Rub harder

remediation.representation: Before-and-after drying photos: water spot vanishes, oil spot stays translucent
remediation.moveShape: Child puts a water drop and an oil drop on paper, waits, and explains which patch stayed

items.prompt_en: In the starch test, what colour shows that starch is present?
items.prompt_hi: Starch test mein kaunsa rang dikhata hai ki starch maujood hai?
items.answer: Blue-black.
hints: Ask what happened to the potato slice in the lab
Point to iodine's own brown colour as the 'no' result
Prompt: starch turns iodine ___
Assert: blue-black means starch

verified.solverAnswer: Blue-black.

items.prompt_en: How can you test a groundnut for fat using just a piece of paper?
items.prompt_hi: Sirf ek kaagaz se moongphali mein fat hai ya nahi, kaise test karoge?
items.answer: Crush and rub the groundnut on the paper and let it dry; an oily, translucent patch that lets light through and does not dry away shows fat.
acceptable: kaagaz pe ragdo, tel ka daag
hints: Ask what an oily paper looks like against light
Point to waiting for it to dry
Prompt: an oily patch that stays after drying means ___
Assert: rub, dry, look for a translucent patch that stays

verified.solverAnswer: Crush it on paper, rub, dry; a translucent oily patch that stays shows fat.
verified.note: Agrees. Practice: use whole groundnuts only by sight/paper, never taste in lab; peanut allergy is possible, add 'do not eat'.

items.prompt_en: Predict: your teacher puts a drop of dilute iodine on a cut potato and on a slice of cucumber. What will you see on each?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: teacher kate hue aloo aur kheere ke tukde pe patle iodine ki ek boond daalti hain. Dono pe kya dikhega?
items.answer: The potato turns blue-black (it has starch); the cucumber shows little or no blue-black and stays the brownish-yellow colour of iodine (very little starch).
hints: Ask which vegetable feels starchy when cut
Point to iodine's normal colour
Prompt: potato turns ___; cucumber stays ___
Assert: potato blue-black; cucumber little or no change

verified.solverAnswer: Potato turns blue-black; cucumber stays brown/yellow-orange (no starch).

items.prompt_en: Predict: the teacher adds iodine to sugar solution and to rice water (the starchy water from cooking rice). Which turns blue-black?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: teacher cheeni ke ghol aur chawal ke maand mein iodine daalti hain. Kaunsa neela-kaala hoga?
items.answer: Only the rice water. Iodine shows starch; sugar is a carbohydrate but not starch, so it does not turn blue-black.
hints: Ask what is in rice water
Point to starch and sugar being different
Prompt: iodine detects ___, not sugar
Assert: only rice water turns blue-black

verified.solverAnswer: Rice water turns blue-black; sugar solution does not.

items.prompt_en: Predict which of these leaves a patch on paper that stays even after drying: a drop of water, a drop of coconut oil, or crushed coconut.
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo, inme se kaun kaagaz pe aisa daag chhodega jo sookhne ke baad bhi rahe: paani ki boond, nariyal tel ki boond, ya pisa hua nariyal?
items.answer: The coconut oil and the crushed coconut (both contain fat); the water patch dries and disappears.
hints: Ask what happens to a wet spot on paper after an hour
Point to oil soaking in
Prompt: water dries away; fat leaves a ___ patch
Assert: oil and crushed coconut leave a lasting patch

verified.solverAnswer: Coconut oil (and perhaps crushed coconut leaves a patch too since it has oil); water dries away.
verified.note: Agrees (coconut oil and crushed coconut both leave a lasting patch; the prompt reads as single-answer but key lists both).

items.prompt_en: Why do we wait for the paper to dry before deciding that a food has fat?
items.prompt_hi: Kisi khaane mein fat hai, ye decide karne se pehle kaagaz ke sookhne ka intezaar kyon karte hain?
items.answer: Water also makes a wet patch, but it dries and disappears; only an oily patch stays translucent after drying.
hints: Ask what the tomato did to the paper
Point to what is left after drying
Prompt: water patches ___, fat patches ___
Assert: drying separates water from fat

verified.solverAnswer: Water also makes a wet patch that disappears on drying; fat leaves a lasting patch.

items.prompt_en: Milk and rice water both look white. The teacher tests both with iodine and with the protein test. What results would you expect?
items.prompt_hi: Doodh aur chawal ka maand dono safed dikhte hain. Teacher dono ko iodine aur protein test se jaanchti hain. Kya result expect karoge?
items.answer: Rice water turns blue-black with iodine (starch). Milk does not turn blue-black with iodine, but it turns violet in the protein test.
hints: Ask what each liquid comes from
Point to starch in rice and protein in milk
Prompt: rice water → ___ with iodine; milk → ___ in the protein test
Assert: looking alike doesn't mean the same nutrients

verified.solverAnswer: Milk: no starch (no blue-black), protein positive (violet); rice water: starch positive, no protein.

items.prompt_en: In the lab, your teacher tests a piece of paneer: iodine shows no blue-black, the paper shows an oily patch, and the protein test turns violet. What nutrients does paneer have?
items.prompt_hi: Lab mein teacher ne paneer ka tukda test kiya: iodine se neela-kaala nahi hua, kaagaz pe tel ka daag aaya, aur protein test baingani hua. Paneer mein kaun se poshak tatva hain?
items.answer: Fat and protein (and little or no starch).
hints: Ask them to read each result one by one
Point to violet and the oily patch
Prompt: oily patch → ___; violet → ___
Assert: paneer has fat and protein

verified.solverAnswer: Fat and protein, no starch.

items.prompt_en: A packet of chips says 'no added fat'. How could you check with a paper test whether the chips still have oil in them?
items.prompt_hi: Chips ke packet pe likha hai 'no added fat'. Kaagaz wale test se kaise check karoge ki chips mein ab bhi tel hai ya nahi?
items.answer: Crush a chip and rub it on paper, let it dry, and hold it to the light; an oily translucent patch that stays means the chips contain fat.
hints: Ask how the groundnut test worked
Point to waiting for drying
Prompt: crush, rub, ___, then look for a ___ patch
Assert: an oily patch after drying shows fat is present

verified.solverAnswer: Rub chips on paper, dry; oily patch means fat.

items.prompt_en: Here are lab results in words: potato turned blue-black with iodine; groundnut gave an oily patch and turned violet; egg white turned violet only. Make a table with columns starch, fat and protein and fill in ✓ or ✗ from these results.
items.prompt_hi: Lab ke results shabdon mein: aloo iodine se neela-kaala hua; moongphali ne tel ka daag diya aur baingani hui; ande ki safedi sirf baingani hui. Starch, fat aur protein ke columns wali table banao aur in results se ✓ ya ✗ bharo.
items.answer: Potato: starch ✓, fat ✗, protein ✗. Groundnut: starch ✗, fat ✓, protein ✓. Egg white: starch ✗, fat ✗, protein ✓.
hints: Invite them to draw the three columns first
Point to one result per row at a time
Prompt: violet goes in the ___ column
Assert: potato starch; groundnut fat and protein; egg white protein

verified.solverAnswer: Potato: starch yes only; groundnut: fat yes, protein yes; egg white: protein only.

items.prompt_en: Golu's notebook says: 'Groundnut gave an oily patch, so groundnut has only fat. No need for the protein test.' What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Golu ki notebook mein likha hai: 'Moongphali ne tel ka daag diya, matlab moongphali mein sirf fat hai. Protein test ki zaroorat nahi.' Galti kya hai?
items.answer: One food can have more than one nutrient; groundnut also has protein. Each nutrient needs its own test.
hints: Ask what the violet test showed for groundnut
Point to the word 'only'
Prompt: one food can have ___ nutrients
Assert: groundnut has fat and protein; test each nutrient

verified.solverAnswer: One nutrient test doesn't exclude others; foods contain several nutrients; must do protein test.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a classmate who was absent how to test foods for starch and for fat, and give one safety rule.
items.prompt_hi: Jo classmate absent tha, use samjhao ki khaane mein starch aur fat kaise test karte hain, aur ek safety rule bhi batao.
items.answer: Key ideas: starch: put a few drops of dilute iodine on the food; blue-black means starch. Fat: rub the food on paper and let it dry; an oily translucent patch means fat. Safety: do chemical tests only with a teacher and never eat tested food or taste chemicals.
hints: Invite them to explain the starch test first
Point to the drying step for fat
Prompt: iodine → ___; oily patch after drying → ___
Assert: two tests plus a safety rule

verified.solverAnswer: Starch: drop iodine, blue-black. Fat: rub on paper, oily patch after drying. Safety: dont taste lab chemicals, iodine stains/poisonous, wash hands.

items.prompt_en: From last time: in the protein test your teacher did, what colour shows protein?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: teacher ne jo protein test kiya, usme kaunsa rang protein dikhata hai?
items.answer: Violet (purple).
hints: Ask them to recall the egg white test
Point to the colour change in the test tube
Prompt: protein shows a ___ colour
Assert: violet means protein

verified.solverAnswer: Violet (purple).

workedExample.problem: Find out whether a boiled potato has starch and fat.
steps: Starch test, with the teacher: put 2-3 drops of dilute iodine solution on a potato slice
Observe: the slice turns blue-black, so starch is present
Fat test: rub a small piece on paper and let the paper dry
Observe: no oily translucent patch remains, so there is little or no fat
Record both results in a table; do not eat the tested food
fadedVersion: Starch test, with the teacher: put 2-3 drops of dilute ___ on a potato slice
Observe: the slice turns ___, so starch is present
Fat test: rub a small piece on ___ and let it dry
Observe: no ___ patch remains, so there is little or no fat
Record both results in a ___; do not eat the tested food

skills.title: Describe a balanced diet: all nutrients, fibre and water in the right amounts
Link deficiency diseases to the missing nutrient and to foods that prevent them
Explain the value of millets and plan a balanced local meal

expectations: A balanced diet has all nutrients, fibre and water in the right amounts for the body's needs; variety matters, not just quantity.

A long-term lack of a nutrient causes a deficiency disease: vitamin C → scurvy (bleeding gums); vitamin D → rickets (soft, bent bones); vitamin A → night blindness; iron → anaemia (tiredness, pale skin); iodine → goitre (swelling in the neck).
Deficiency diseases are not caught from others; they are prevented by eating the right foods (sunlight on the skin helps the body make vitamin D).
Millets like ragi, jowar and bajra are nutritious (rich in fibre and minerals, such as calcium in ragi and iron in bajra), need less water and grow well in dry regions.
Eating too much, especially fried, sugary or salty food, can cause obesity and other problems; more food is not always better.

misconceptions.belief: Eating more food always means better health.
signs: Says 'eat more, become strong'
Thinks a fatter child is always healthier
Equates big portions with a good diet

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which is healthier for a child?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Bachche ke liye kya zyada healthy hai?

options.text: Eating a lot of one food, like a big plate of rice, every day
Eating a variety of foods in the right amounts
Eating as many sweets as possible for energy

remediation.representation: Two plates of the same size: one heap of rice vs a varied thali
remediation.moveShape: Child lists what each plate gives and what each is missing; size is held equal so variety stands out

misconceptions.belief: Deficiency diseases are caught from other people like a cold.
signs: Says scurvy or anaemia spreads
Wants to stay away from a friend with anaemia

diagnostic.prompt_en: Riya's gums bleed and the doctor says she lacks vitamin C. How did she get this?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Riya ke masoodon se khoon aata hai aur doctor kehti hain use vitamin C ki kami hai. Use ye kaise hua?

options.text: She caught it from a friend
She has not been eating enough vitamin C foods like amla, guava and lemon
From drinking too much water

remediation.representation: Two-column card: 'caught from germs' vs 'caused by a missing nutrient'
remediation.moveShape: Sort a cold, scurvy, anaemia and chickenpox into the columns; child explains how each is prevented

misconceptions.belief: Millets are old-fashioned 'poor people's food' and less nutritious than polished rice or wheat.
signs: Refuses ragi or bajra
Says rice is 'proper' food
Thinks millets have no nutrients

diagnostic.prompt_en: Compared with polished white rice, ragi has…
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Safed polish wale chawal ke mukaable, ragi mein…

options.text: much more calcium and fibre
no nutrients at all
only water

remediation.representation: Bar comparison of calcium and fibre: ragi vs white rice
remediation.moveShape: Child predicts the bars before reveal, then names one dish from their region using a millet

items.prompt_en: What is a balanced diet?
items.prompt_hi: Santulit aahaar (balanced diet) kya hota hai?
items.answer: A diet that has all the nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins and minerals), fibre and water in the right amounts for the body's needs.
acceptable: sab poshak tatva sahi matra mein
hints: Ask what was on a varied thali
Point to the words 'all' and 'right amount'
Prompt: a balanced diet has ___ nutrients in the ___ amounts
Assert: all nutrients, fibre and water, in the right amounts

verified.solverAnswer: A diet that has all nutrients in right amounts from a variety of foods.

items.prompt_en: Match each disease to the missing nutrient: night blindness, goitre, anaemia, scurvy.
items.prompt_hi: Har bimari ko kami wale poshak tatva se milao: raatondhi (night blindness), ghenga (goitre), khoon ki kami (anaemia), scurvy.
items.answer: Night blindness: vitamin A. Goitre: iodine. Anaemia: iron. Scurvy: vitamin C.
hints: Ask which one is linked to iodised salt
Point to amla for scurvy
Prompt: anaemia is a lack of ___
Assert: A-night blindness, iodine-goitre, iron-anaemia, C-scurvy

verified.solverAnswer: Night blindness: vitamin A; goitre: iodine; anaemia: iron; scurvy: vitamin C.

items.prompt_en: Long ago, sailors spent months at sea eating only dry biscuits and salted meat, with no fresh fruit. Predict which illness many of them got, and what would have prevented it.
items.prompt_hi: Bahut pehle naavik mahino samundar mein sirf sookhe biscuit aur namak lage meat pe rehte the, taaza phal bilkul nahi. Guess karo unme se kai logon ko kaunsi bimari hui, aur kya karne se bachte?
items.answer: Scurvy (bleeding gums, weakness) from lack of vitamin C; fresh fruits such as lemons, oranges or amla would have prevented it.
hints: Ask what fresh fruit gives that biscuits don't
Point to bleeding gums as the sign
Prompt: no fresh fruit means no vitamin ___
Assert: scurvy; fresh citrus or amla prevents it

verified.solverAnswer: Scurvy; prevented by fresh fruits/vitamin C foods like citrus.

items.prompt_en: Two children eat the same total amount daily. Child A eats only rice. Child B eats rice, dal, vegetables, fruit and milk. Predict who will be healthier after a few months, and why.
items.prompt_hi: Do bachche roz utna hi khaana khaate hain. Bachcha A sirf chawal khaata hai. Bachcha B chawal, dal, sabzi, phal aur doodh. Guess karo kuch mahino baad kaun zyada healthy hoga, aur kyon?
items.answer: Child B. Child A gets mostly carbohydrates and lacks proteins, vitamins, minerals and fibre, so may grow poorly, feel weak and develop deficiencies.
hints: Ask what rice alone gives
Point to what is missing from A's plate
Prompt: same amount, but B gets more ___
Assert: B is healthier; variety beats quantity

verified.solverAnswer: Child B, variety gives all nutrients.

items.prompt_en: In a dry year with little rain, a farmer in Rajasthan plants bajra in one field and rice in another. Predict which crop is more likely to do well.
items.prompt_hi: Kam baarish wale saal mein Rajasthan ka ek kisaan ek khet mein bajra aur doosre mein chawal lagata hai. Guess karo kaunsi fasal achhi hogi.
items.answer: Bajra; millets need much less water and tolerate heat and dry soil, while rice needs a lot of water.
hints: Ask how much water a rice field needs
Point to millets growing in dry regions
Prompt: millets need ___ water
Assert: bajra does better in a dry year

verified.solverAnswer: Bajra, millets drought tolerant.

items.prompt_en: Why is iodised salt (salt with added iodine) used in most Indian homes?
items.prompt_hi: Zyada-tar Bharatiya gharon mein iodine wala namak kyon use hota hai?
items.answer: To prevent iodine deficiency, which causes goitre; the body needs iodine for the thyroid gland, and many foods and soils have too little of it.
hints: Ask which disease is linked to iodine
Point to the swelling in the neck
Prompt: iodised salt prevents ___
Assert: it prevents goitre by supplying iodine

verified.solverAnswer: Prevent iodine deficiency/goitre.

items.prompt_en: Compare two breakfasts: a ragi dosa with chutney and a glass of milk, and a packet of chips with a cold drink. Which is closer to balanced, and why?
items.prompt_hi: Do naashte compare karo: ragi dosa chutney ke saath aur ek glass doodh, ya chips ka packet aur cold drink. Kaunsa balanced ke zyada kareeb hai, aur kyon?
items.answer: The ragi dosa and milk: it gives carbohydrates, protein, calcium and fibre. Chips and a cold drink give mostly fat, salt and sugar, with little protein, vitamins or fibre.
hints: Ask what each breakfast gives
Point to salt and sugar in the second
Prompt: ragi gives calcium and ___; chips give mostly ___ and salt
Assert: ragi dosa with milk is closer to balanced

verified.solverAnswer: Ragi dosa with milk is closer to balanced; chips and cold drink are fat/sugar/salt with little nutrition.

items.prompt_en: Your friend often feels tired, looks pale and gets breathless while playing. A doctor finds she lacks iron. Suggest three foods she could eat more of.
items.prompt_hi: Tumhari dost aksar thaki rehti hai, peeli dikhti hai aur khelte hue saans phoolti hai. Doctor ko pata chala use iron ki kami hai. Teen khaane batao jo use zyada khaane chahiye.
items.answer: Any three: green leafy vegetables (palak, methi), jaggery, bajra or ragi, pulses and chana, dates, eggs or meat if she eats them; vitamin C foods like amla help the body absorb iron.
hints: Ask what anaemia is a lack of
Point to dark green leafy vegetables
Prompt: iron-rich foods include palak, ___ and ___
Assert: leafy greens, jaggery, millets, pulses are iron-rich

verified.solverAnswer: Spinach (palak), jaggery, dal/rajma, meat/liver, dates.

items.prompt_en: Plan one balanced lunch for a family in your region using at least one millet. Name each food and the nutrient it mainly gives.
items.prompt_hi: Apne ilaake ke ek parivaar ke liye ek balanced lunch plan karo jisme kam se kam ek millet ho. Har khaana aur uska mukhya poshak tatva batao.
items.answer: Any balanced plan with a millet, e.g.: bajra roti (carbohydrate, iron, fibre), dal (protein), palak sabzi (vitamins, minerals, fibre), curd (protein, calcium), salad (vitamins, fibre), a little ghee (fat) and water.
hints: Invite them to start with the millet dish
Point to each nutrient group still missing
Prompt: millet roti, plus a protein like ___, plus a vegetable for ___
Assert: a millet base plus protein, vegetables, a little fat and water

verified.solverAnswer: Bajra roti (energy, fibre), dal (protein), sabzi (vitamins), curd (calcium/protein), ghee.

items.prompt_en: Draw a table with three columns: nutrient, disease if missing, food that prevents it. Fill in rows for vitamin A, vitamin D and iron.
items.prompt_hi: Teen column wali table banao: poshak tatva, kami se bimari, bachane wala khaana. Vitamin A, vitamin D aur iron ki rows bharo.
items.answer: Vitamin A: night blindness: carrot, papaya, mango, green leafy vegetables. Vitamin D: rickets: sunlight, milk, eggs. Iron: anaemia: green leafy vegetables, jaggery, bajra, pulses.
hints: Invite them to fill the disease column first
Point to sunlight as a source of vitamin D
Prompt: vitamin D → ___ → sunlight and milk
Assert: A-night blindness-carrot; D-rickets-sunlight; iron-anaemia-greens

verified.solverAnswer: Vitamin A: night blindness: carrot, papaya, milk. Vitamin D: rickets: sunlight, milk, eggs. Iron: anaemia: spinach, jaggery.

items.prompt_en: Golu says: 'I eat five parathas with lots of butter every morning, so I'm eating a balanced diet.' What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Main roz subah bahut saare makkhan ke saath paanch parathe khaata hoon, isliye mera diet balanced hai.' Galti kya hai?
items.answer: A lot of food is not the same as balance: this is mostly carbohydrate and fat, lacking protein, vitamins, minerals and fibre, and too much fat can lead to obesity.
hints: Ask what is missing from his plate
Point to the amount of butter
Prompt: balance means ___, not just more
Assert: big portions of two nutrients aren't balanced

verified.solverAnswer: Only carbs and fat; no variety (proteins, vitamins, minerals, fibre); too much fat.

items.prompt_en: Explain to your grandparents why schools and the government are encouraging millets again.
items.prompt_hi: Apne daada-daadi ya naana-naani ko samjhao ki school aur sarkar phir se millets ko badhava kyon de rahe hain.
items.answer: Key ideas: millets like ragi, jowar and bajra are rich in fibre and minerals (ragi has calcium, bajra has iron); they need little water and grow in dry, poor soils; they are good for health and for farmers in dry areas; 2023 was the International Year of Millets.
hints: Invite them to name millets the family already knows
Point to water needs and nutrients
Prompt: millets are rich in ___ and need less ___
Assert: nutritious, water-saving, suited to dry farming

verified.solverAnswer: Millets are nutritious (fibre, minerals), drought tolerant, need little water, good for farmers and health.

items.prompt_en: From last time: a child with soft, bent leg bones may lack which vitamin, and what free source helps the body make it?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: naram, mudi hui haddiyon wale bachche mein kis vitamin ki kami ho sakti hai, aur kaunsa muft source shareer ko ise banane mein madad karta hai?
items.answer: Vitamin D (the disease is rickets); sunlight on the skin.
hints: Ask what the bone disease is called
Point to sitting in morning sunshine
Prompt: rickets is a lack of vitamin ___
Assert: vitamin D, made with the help of sunlight

verified.solverAnswer: Vitamin D (rickets); sunlight.

workedExample.problem: Check whether Aman's lunch of rice and potato sabzi is balanced, and fix it.
steps: List what is there: rice and potato give mainly carbohydrates; the oil gives fat
Find what is missing: proteins, vitamins and minerals, and fibre
Add a protein food: dal or curd
Add protective foods: a green vegetable or salad, and a fruit
Check amounts and variety: not too much oil; drink water
fadedVersion: List what is there: rice and potato give mainly ___
Find what is missing: ___, vitamins and minerals, and fibre
Add a protein food: ___ or curd
Add protective foods: a green vegetable or ___
Check amounts and variety: not too much ___; drink water

skills.title: Define food miles and find out where foods come from
Compare foods by distance travelled and explain the effects on fuel, pollution and freshness
Suggest ways to reduce food miles and recognise their limits

expectations: Food miles are the distance food travels from where it is grown or made to where it is eaten.
Food that travels far uses more fuel for trucks, trains, ships or planes, which adds to air pollution; it may also need cold storage, packaging or preservatives and can lose freshness.
Local and seasonal food usually travels less, is fresher and supports nearby farmers.
The source of food matters, so we can read labels and ask sellers where food comes from.
Some foods can't be grown everywhere, and distance is only one factor; how food is grown and stored also matters.

misconceptions.belief: Where food comes from does not matter.
signs: Says 'it all comes from the shop'
Cannot name where common foods are grown
Dismisses origin labels

diagnostic.prompt_en: Two bunches of spinach cost the same. One was grown in a village 10 km away; the other was brought from 1500 km away. Which is likely fresher and used less fuel to reach you?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Palak ki do gaddiyan same daam ki hain. Ek 10 km door ke gaon mein ugi, doosri 1500 km door se aayi. Kaunsi zyada taazi hogi aur pahunchne mein kam fuel lagaa?

options.text: They are the same; where food comes from doesn't matter
The one from 10 km away
The one from far away, because it travelled more

remediation.representation: India map with two arrows of very different lengths ending at the child's city
remediation.moveShape: Child draws both arrows and lists what the long journey needs (fuel, cold storage, days)

misconceptions.belief: Food from far away is better or more nutritious because it is imported or special.
signs: Prefers imported fruit as 'better'
Thinks travelling far adds quality

diagnostic.prompt_en: Riya says imported kiwis must be healthier than the guavas in her local market because they come from far away. Is she right?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Riya kehti hai ki imported kiwi local bazaar ke amrood se zyada healthy honge kyonki door se aaye hain. Kya woh sahi hai?

options.text: Yes, food from far away is always better
No; distance doesn't add nutrients, and fresh local guavas are very nutritious (rich in vitamin C)
Yes, because they cost more

remediation.representation: Nutrient card for guava next to the kiwi's journey map
remediation.moveShape: Separate 'how far it came' from 'what it contains'; child compares both cards

misconceptions.belief: Food miles count only the distance from the shop to home.
signs: Says food miles are 'dukaan se ghar'
Ignores the farm-to-market journey

diagnostic.prompt_en: Food miles for an apple bought in Chennai means the distance from…
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Chennai mein khareede gaye seb ke food miles ka matlab hai doori…

options.text: the shop to your house only
the orchard where it grew to your plate
your house to school

remediation.representation: Journey strip: orchard → packing → truck → mandi → shop → home, with the last step tiny
remediation.moveShape: Child adds up each leg and sees the shop-to-home part is the smallest

items.prompt_en: What are 'food miles'?
items.prompt_hi: 'Food miles' kya hote hain?
items.answer: The distance food travels from where it is grown or made to where it is eaten.
acceptable: khet se thali tak ki doori
hints: Ask where their morning banana began its journey
Point to the start and the end of the trip
Prompt: food miles are the distance from the ___ to the ___
Assert: farm-to-plate distance

verified.solverAnswer: Distance food travels from where it is grown to where it is eaten.

items.prompt_en: Pick three foods in your kitchen. Ask an adult or read the packet to find out where each came from.
items.prompt_hi: Apne kitchen ki teen cheezein chuno. Kisi bade se poochh ke ya packet padh ke pata karo ki har ek kahan se aayi.
items.answer: Any three foods with a correct place of origin from a label or an adult, e.g. tea from Assam, apples from Himachal Pradesh, rice from Punjab.
hints: Invite them to look for 'product of' on packets
Point to asking the vegetable seller
Prompt: this ___ came from ___
Assert: labels and sellers tell us where food comes from

verified.solverAnswer: Open-ended: origin of three foods.

items.prompt_en: Predict: an apple from Himachal Pradesh travels by truck to Chennai, and a banana grows on a farm 20 km from Chennai. Which used more fuel to reach the Chennai market?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: Himachal ka seb truck se Chennai jaata hai, aur Chennai se 20 km door ke khet mein kela ugta hai. Chennai ki mandi tak pahunchne mein kisme zyada fuel laga?
items.answer: The apple; it travelled more than 2,000 km, while the banana travelled only about 20 km.
hints: Ask how far Himachal is from Chennai
Point to the length of each journey
Prompt: the longer trip burns more ___
Assert: the apple used far more fuel

verified.solverAnswer: The apple from Himachal.

items.prompt_en: Predict what is needed to keep strawberries fresh on a long, hot journey from far away, and what that adds.
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo, door se lambe garam safar mein strawberry ko taaza rakhne ke liye kya chahiye, aur isse kya badhta hai?
items.answer: Refrigerated trucks or cold storage and special packaging; these use more energy, cost more and create more packaging waste.
hints: Ask what happens to soft fruit in the heat
Point to cooling and boxes
Prompt: long trips need ___ storage and extra ___
Assert: cooling and packaging add energy, cost and waste

verified.solverAnswer: Cold storage/refrigerated transport; adds energy, fuel, cost and pollution.

items.prompt_en: Why does food that travels a long way usually add more pollution?
items.prompt_hi: Jo khaana bahut door se aata hai, woh aam taur pe zyada pradooshan kyon badhata hai?
items.answer: Vehicles burn fuel such as diesel for the whole journey, so longer trips release more smoke and gases; cold storage on the way also uses energy.
hints: Ask what trucks burn to move
Point to the length of the trip
Prompt: more distance → more fuel → more ___
Assert: longer journeys burn more fuel and pollute more

verified.solverAnswer: Transport burns fuel releasing carbon dioxide and pollutants; storage/packaging too.

items.prompt_en: Compare mangoes bought in May from the local mandi with mangoes bought in December that came from very far away. Which are local and seasonal, and what are their advantages?
items.prompt_hi: Mai mein local mandi se khareede aam aur December mein bahut door se aaye aam compare karo. Kaunse local aur mausami hain, aur unke kya fayde hain?
items.answer: The May mangoes are local and seasonal: fresher, usually cheaper, fewer food miles and they support local farmers.
hints: Ask when mangoes grow naturally in India
Point to the journey of December mangoes
Prompt: seasonal local fruit is ___ and travels ___
Assert: May local mangoes: fresh, cheaper, fewer food miles

verified.solverAnswer: May local seasonal mango; fresher, cheaper, less fuel, tastier. December far mangoes have long travel.

items.prompt_en: Your family's tea packet says 'Product of Assam'. If you live in Jaipur, are its food miles short or long? Why?
items.prompt_hi: Ghar ki chai ke packet pe likha hai 'Product of Assam'. Agar tum Jaipur mein rehte ho, toh iske food miles kam hain ya zyada? Kyon?
items.answer: Long; Assam is in the far north-east, well over 1,500 km from Jaipur, so the tea travels a long way.
hints: Ask where Assam is on the map
Point to the distance across the country
Prompt: Assam to Jaipur is more than ___ km
Assert: long food miles, crossing much of India

verified.solverAnswer: Long (Assam to Jaipur is about 2000 km).

items.prompt_en: Your school wants to cut food miles for its mid-day meal. Suggest three practical ideas.
items.prompt_hi: Tumhara school mid-day meal ke food miles kam karna chahta hai. Teen practical idea batao.
items.answer: Any three: buy vegetables and grains from nearby farmers; use seasonal produce; grow a school kitchen garden; use local millets; reduce packaged foods.
hints: Ask where the school's vegetables come from now
Point to the school's own land
Prompt: buy ___, cook ___ food, grow a ___
Assert: local, seasonal, home-grown, less packaged

verified.solverAnswer: Buy local vegetables, seasonal food, school garden, local farmers, millets.

items.prompt_en: On a map of India, draw an arrow showing apples coming from Himachal Pradesh to Chennai, and another showing bananas coming from a farm near Chennai. Which arrow is longer, and what does arrow length stand for?
items.prompt_hi: India ke map pe ek teer banao jo Himachal se Chennai tak seb aate dikhaye, aur doosra jo Chennai ke paas ke khet se kele aate dikhaye. Kaunsa teer lamba hai, aur teer ki lambai kya dikhati hai?
items.answer: The apple arrow is much longer; arrow length stands for food miles (distance travelled).
hints: Invite them to mark both starting points first
Point to the end at Chennai
Prompt: a longer arrow means more ___
Assert: apple arrow longer; length shows food miles

verified.solverAnswer: Himachal to Chennai arrow longer; length stands for food miles/distance.

items.prompt_en: Golu says: 'Food miles are just the distance from the shop to my house, so my food miles are only 1 km.' Fix Golu's idea.
items.prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Food miles bas dukaan se mere ghar tak ki doori hai, isliye mere food miles sirf 1 km hain.' Golu ki soch theek karo.
items.answer: Food miles count the whole journey from the farm or factory to the plate; the 1 km from the shop is only the last small part.
hints: Ask where the shop got the food from
Point to the farm at the start
Prompt: food miles start at the ___
Assert: the whole farm-to-plate trip counts

verified.solverAnswer: Food miles are from where it was grown/produced to where eaten, whole journey.

items.prompt_en: Explain to your family why choosing local and seasonal fruit is good, and when it is still fine to buy food from far away.
items.prompt_hi: Apne parivaar ko samjhao ki local aur mausami phal chunna achha kyon hai, aur kab door se aaya khaana lena bhi theek hai.
items.answer: Key ideas: local and seasonal food has fewer food miles, needs less fuel and causes less pollution, is fresher and supports local farmers; it is fine to buy from far away when a food cannot be grown nearby and is needed for a balanced diet.
hints: Invite them to start with one local fruit they like
Point to foods that can't grow in their area
Prompt: local food is fresher and uses less ___
Assert: prefer local and seasonal; distant food is fine when needed

verified.solverAnswer: Local seasonal: fresher, less transport pollution, supports farmers; far is fine when it can't be grown nearby (e.g. tea, spices) or fresh need.

items.prompt_en: From last time: give two problems caused when food travels very long distances.
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: jab khaana bahut lambi doori tay karta hai, toh do samasyaayein batao.
items.answer: Any two: more fuel burnt and more air pollution; it loses freshness; it needs cold storage, packaging or preservatives; it can cost more.
hints: Ask what the apple's long trip needed
Point to fuel and freshness
Prompt: long trips mean more ___ and less ___
Assert: more fuel and pollution, less freshness

verified.solverAnswer: Pollution/fuel use, spoilage, higher cost, need for storage.

workedExample.problem: Compare the food miles of apples from Shimla and spinach from a farm near Delhi, for a family in Delhi.
steps: Find where each food grows: apples in Shimla, spinach on a farm just outside Delhi
Find each distance to Delhi using a map: about 350 km for the apples, about 20 km for the spinach
Compare: the apples travelled more than 15 times as far
Link: more distance means more fuel, more pollution and less freshness
Choose: prefer the local spinach; buy apples in their season when they are freshest
fadedVersion: Find where each food grows: apples in ___, spinach near Delhi
Find each distance using a ___: about 350 km and about 20 km
Compare: the apples travelled more than ___ times as far
Link: more distance means more ___, more pollution and less freshness
Choose: prefer the ___ spinach; buy apples in their season

skills.title: Test objects with a magnet and record attracted or not attracted
Name magnetic materials (iron, nickel, cobalt, many steels) and non-magnetic ones (aluminium, copper, brass, plastic, wood, glass)
Explain that only some metals are magnetic and use magnets to sort or separate

expectations: A magnet attracts objects made of magnetic materials such as iron, nickel and cobalt, and steels that contain iron.
Many metals are non-magnetic: aluminium, copper, brass, gold and silver; non-metals like plastic, wood, paper, rubber and glass are also non-magnetic.
Being shiny or metal-looking does not mean an object is magnetic; we have to test it.
Some stainless steels are not attracted to a magnet, so two steel spoons can give different results.
Magnetic force acts through paper, cloth, glass and water.
Magnets help separate iron from other materials, for example iron scrap from aluminium cans.

misconceptions.belief: Magnets attract all metals, including aluminium, copper and brass.
signs: Predicts aluminium foil or a copper wire will stick
Says 'it's metal, so it will stick'
Uses the magnet test to decide whether something is a metal

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which of these will stick to a magnet?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Inme se kaunsi cheez magnet se chipkegi?

options.text: An aluminium pan
A copper wire
An iron nail

remediation.representation: Metal line-up test card: iron, steel, aluminium, copper, brass with a magnet icon per row
remediation.moveShape: Child predicts each row, tests, and circles the surprises; ask what the attracted ones have in common

misconceptions.belief: A magnet works only by direct touch and cannot act through paper, water or cloth.
signs: Says the magnet won't work through a notebook page
Removes covers before testing

diagnostic.prompt_en: A paper clip lies on top of a sheet of paper. You move a magnet underneath the paper. What happens?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kaagaz ke upar ek paper clip rakhi hai. Tum kaagaz ke neeche magnet ghumaate ho. Kya hoga?

options.text: Nothing; magnets can't act through paper
The paper clip moves along with the magnet, because magnetic force acts through paper
The paper sticks to the magnet

remediation.representation: Layer test: paper, cloth, cardboard, a glass of water between magnet and clip
remediation.moveShape: Child adds layers one at a time and notes when the pull finally stops

misconceptions.belief: Everything made of steel behaves the same with a magnet.
signs: Is surprised when a steel spoon doesn't stick
Assumes every steel tumbler is magnetic

diagnostic.prompt_en: Two shiny steel spoons: one sticks to a magnet, the other doesn't. Why?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Do chamakdaar steel ki chammach: ek magnet se chipakti hai, doosri nahi. Kyon?

options.text: The magnet is broken
They are made of different kinds of steel; some stainless steels are not magnetic
All steel is the same, so one of them must secretly be aluminium

remediation.representation: Kitchen drawer test log with a 'steel: sticks / doesn't' column
remediation.moveShape: Child tests several steel items at home and reports the mix; normalise that 'steel' is a family of materials

items.prompt_en: Using a fridge magnet, test five things at home, like a steel spoon, a plastic bottle cap, an iron safety pin, a door key and a pencil. Tell me which ones stuck.
items.prompt_hi: Fridge magnet se ghar ki paanch cheezein test karo, jaise steel ki chammach, plastic ka dhakkan, safety pin, chaabi aur pencil. Batao kaunsi chipki.
items.answer: Iron or steel things like safety pins and paper clips stick; plastic, wood and pencils don't; brass keys don't; a steel spoon may or may not, depending on the kind of steel.
hints: Invite them to predict before each test
Point to the golden key and the shiny spoon
Prompt: iron things ___, plastic ___
Assert: iron and many steels stick; plastic, wood, brass don't

verified.solverAnswer: Steel spoon (some stick), iron safety pin sticks, door key (depends; brass no, iron/steel yes); plastic cap, pencil do not.

items.prompt_en: Name three materials a magnet attracts and three it does not.
items.prompt_hi: Teen materials batao jinhe magnet kheenchta hai aur teen jinhe nahi.
items.answer: Attracts: iron, nickel, cobalt (and steels containing iron). Does not attract (any three): aluminium, copper, brass, plastic, wood, glass, paper, rubber.
hints: Ask what a safety pin is made of
Point to the aluminium pan in the kitchen
Prompt: magnets attract iron, ___ and ___
Assert: iron, nickel, cobalt yes; aluminium, copper, plastic no

verified.solverAnswer: Attracted: iron, nickel, cobalt/steel. Not: plastic, wood, rubber, copper, aluminium.

items.prompt_en: Before testing, predict: will a magnet pick up a piece of aluminium foil? An iron nail? A copper wire?
items.prompt_hi: Test karne se pehle guess karo: kya magnet aluminium foil uthayega? Lohe ki keel? Taambe ka taar?
items.answer: Only the iron nail; aluminium and copper are metals but they are not magnetic.
hints: Ask which of the three is iron
Point to all three being metals
Prompt: only ___ is magnetic here
Assert: only the iron nail; aluminium and copper are non-magnetic metals

verified.solverAnswer: Aluminium foil: no; iron nail: yes; copper wire: no.

items.prompt_en: Predict: a golden-yellow house key made of brass. Will it stick to a magnet?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: peetal ki bani sunehri ghar ki chaabi. Kya woh magnet se chipkegi?
items.answer: No; brass (made of copper and zinc) is not magnetic.
hints: Ask what brass is made of
Point to copper being non-magnetic
Prompt: brass is a metal but it is ___
Assert: brass keys don't stick

verified.solverAnswer: No, brass is not magnetic.

items.prompt_en: A paper clip is at the bottom of a glass of water. Predict: can you drag it up the side of the glass without touching the water, by moving a strong magnet outside the glass?
items.prompt_hi: Paani ke glass ke andar neeche ek paper clip padi hai. Guess karo: kya bahar se tez magnet ghuma kar, paani ko chhoo-e bina, clip ko glass ki deewar ke saath upar la sakte ho?
items.answer: Yes; magnetic force acts through glass and water, so the clip follows the magnet.
hints: Ask whether the paper test worked through paper
Point to glass and water as more layers
Prompt: magnetic force can act through ___ and water
Assert: yes, the clip follows the magnet

verified.solverAnswer: Yes, magnet acts through glass and water.

items.prompt_en: You correctly said aluminium foil won't stick. Why not, if it is a metal?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne sahi kaha ki aluminium foil nahi chipkegi. Agar woh dhaatu hai toh kyon nahi?
items.answer: Only some metals are magnetic (iron, nickel, cobalt and alloys like steel that contain them); aluminium is a non-magnetic metal.
hints: Ask which metals did stick
Point to 'some metals, not all'
Prompt: magnets attract only ___ metals
Assert: aluminium is a non-magnetic metal

verified.solverAnswer: Only some metals (iron, nickel, cobalt) are magnetic; aluminium isn't.

items.prompt_en: An iron safety pin and an aluminium hair clip both look silvery and shiny. How can you tell them apart without scratching or tasting them?
items.prompt_hi: Lohe ki safety pin aur aluminium ka hair clip dono chandi jaise chamakte hain. Bina khurche ya chakhe dono ko kaise alag pehchaanoge?
items.answer: Test with a magnet: the iron pin is attracted, the aluminium clip is not.
hints: Ask which property differs between iron and aluminium
Point to the magnet in hand
Prompt: a magnet pulls the ___ but not the ___
Assert: magnet test separates them

verified.solverAnswer: Test with a magnet: the pin sticks, aluminium doesn't.

items.prompt_en: A kabadiwala has a heap of mixed steel food tins and aluminium drink cans. How could he quickly separate them?
items.prompt_hi: Ek kabadiwale ke paas steel ke dabbe aur aluminium ke cold drink ke cans ka mila hua dher hai. Woh jaldi se inhe kaise alag karega?
items.answer: Use a strong magnet: the steel tins are pulled out and the aluminium cans are left behind.
hints: Ask which of the two is magnetic
Point to sweeping a magnet over the heap
Prompt: the magnet picks up the ___, leaves the ___
Assert: a magnet pulls out the steel tins

verified.solverAnswer: Use a magnet; steel tins stick, aluminium cans don't.
verified.note: Agrees. Hint 2 already states the method (sweeping a magnet over the heap).

items.prompt_en: Sand from a river bank sometimes has tiny black grains that stick to a magnet wrapped in a plastic bag. What might those grains contain?
items.prompt_hi: Nadi kinare ki ret mein kabhi-kabhi chhote kaale daane hote hain jo plastic bag mein lipte magnet se chipak jaate hain. Un daanon mein kya ho sakta hai?
items.answer: Iron (an iron-containing mineral), since only magnetic materials like iron are attracted.
hints: Ask what kind of material sticks to magnets
Point to the black colour as a clue
Prompt: if it sticks, it likely contains ___
Assert: the grains contain iron

verified.solverAnswer: Iron (magnetite) particles.

items.prompt_en: Make a two-column chart, 'Attracted' and 'Not attracted', and place: iron nail, plastic scale, steel paper clip, copper wire, rubber eraser, nickel strip.
items.prompt_hi: Do column ka chart banao, 'Kheencha gaya' aur 'Nahi kheencha gaya', aur rakho: lohe ki keel, plastic scale, steel paper clip, taambe ka taar, rubber, nickel ki patti.
items.answer: Attracted: iron nail, steel paper clip, nickel strip. Not attracted: plastic scale, copper wire, rubber eraser.
acceptable: attracted iron nail paper clip nickel
hints: Invite them to sort the obvious ones first
Point to copper and nickel as the tricky pair
Prompt: nickel goes in ___; copper goes in ___
Assert: iron, steel clip, nickel attracted; plastic, copper, rubber not

verified.solverAnswer: Attracted: iron nail, steel paper clip, nickel strip. Not: plastic scale, copper wire, eraser.

items.prompt_en: Golu wrote: 'All metals stick to magnets; that's how we know if something is a metal.' Find his mistake.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ne likha: 'Saari dhaatuein magnet se chipakti hain; isi se pata chalta hai ki koi cheez dhaatu hai.' Uski galti dhundho.
items.answer: Many metals (aluminium, copper, brass, gold, silver) do not stick; a magnet test shows whether something is magnetic, not whether it is a metal.
hints: Ask about the aluminium foil test
Point to the brass key
Prompt: the magnet test shows ___, not 'metal'
Assert: only some metals are magnetic

verified.solverAnswer: Not all metals are magnetic; aluminium, copper, gold, silver aren't.

items.prompt_en: Explain to your younger cousin which things a magnet can pick up, and why 'shiny metal' isn't enough to know.
items.prompt_hi: Apne chhote cousin ko samjhao ki magnet kaunsi cheezein utha sakta hai, aur 'chamakdaar dhaatu' hona kaafi kyon nahi hai.
items.answer: Key ideas: magnets attract iron, nickel, cobalt and many steels; they don't attract aluminium, copper, brass, plastic or wood; shiny doesn't mean magnetic, so test it; even some steel spoons don't stick.
hints: Invite them to start with something that sticks and something that doesn't
Point to the shiny aluminium foil
Prompt: magnets attract ___ but not aluminium or ___
Assert: only some materials are magnetic; test, don't guess

verified.solverAnswer: Magnets pick up iron, nickel, cobalt things; many shiny metals (aluminium, copper) aren't magnetic.

items.prompt_en: From last time: name one metal that is NOT attracted by a magnet.
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek aisi dhaatu batao jise magnet nahi kheenchta.
items.answer: Any one: aluminium, copper, brass, gold, silver.
hints: Ask what the foil was made of
Point to the copper wire
Prompt: aluminium and ___ are not magnetic
Assert: e.g. aluminium or copper

verified.solverAnswer: Aluminium (or copper).

workedExample.problem: Sort these kitchen things with a magnet: a cold iron tawa, aluminium foil, a steel spoon, a plastic lid.
steps: Predict for each item first and write it down
Test each one with the magnet, one at a time
Record: tawa attracted; foil not attracted; steel spoon attracted or not, depending on its steel; plastic lid not attracted
Group them into magnetic and non-magnetic
Conclude: only some metals are magnetic, and looking shiny is not enough to tell

Test each one with the ___, one at a time

skills.title: Locate the poles of a magnet, where the attraction is strongest
State that like poles repel and unlike poles attract, and use repulsion as the sure test of a magnet
Explain that strength is not size, that broken magnets form new poles, and how to care for magnets

expectations: Every magnet has two poles, north and south; the attraction is strongest at the poles, which is why iron filings cluster at the ends.
Like poles repel each other; unlike poles attract.
Repulsion is the sure test that an object is a magnet; attraction alone may just mean the object is made of iron.
If a magnet is broken, each piece becomes a complete magnet with its own north and south pole; a single pole cannot be separated.
A bigger magnet is not always stronger; strength depends on the material and how it was magnetised.
Magnets can lose their magnetism if heated, hammered or dropped often, so they are stored in pairs with unlike poles side by side and keepers across the ends.

misconceptions.belief: A bigger magnet is always stronger.
signs: Picks the biggest magnet without testing
Compares magnets by size alone

diagnostic.prompt_en: A small thin magnet lifts 20 pins; a big grey magnet lifts only 8. What does this show?

Both a north and a south pole; each half is a complete magnet
No poles; broken magnets stop working

options.text: Evenly all along the magnet
Mostly at the middle
Mostly near the two ends (the poles)

Never checks for repulsion

No; it might just be iron. If one of its ends is pushed away by a magnet's pole, then it is a magnet
No, magnets never attract each other

items.prompt_en: Where on a bar magnet is the pull strongest?
items.prompt_hi: Bar magnet mein kheenchne ki taakat sabse zyada kahan hoti hai?
items.answer: At its two ends, the poles.

Point to the ends of the magnet
Prompt: the pull is strongest at the ___
Assert: at the two poles

verified.solverAnswer: At the poles (the ends).

items.prompt_en: What happens when you bring the north pole of one magnet near the south pole of another? And north near north?
items.prompt_hi: Ek magnet ka north pole doosre ke south pole ke paas laao toh kya hota hai? Aur north ke paas north?
items.answer: North and south attract each other; north and north repel each other.
hints: Ask which pair felt like a pull and which a push
Point to 'like' and 'unlike'
Prompt: like poles ___, unlike poles ___
Assert: unlike attract; like repel

verified.solverAnswer: N near S attract; N near N repel.

items.prompt_en: Predict: in the school lab, your teacher places a sheet of paper over a bar magnet and sprinkles iron filings on it. Where will the filings gather the most?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: school lab mein teacher bar magnet ke upar ek kaagaz rakh ke uspe lohe ka buraada chhidakti hain. Buraada sabse zyada kahan jama hoga?
items.answer: At the two ends (the poles), with far fewer in the middle.
hints: Ask where the magnet held most pins
Point to the ends and the middle
Prompt: filings crowd at the ___
Assert: most filings gather at the poles

verified.solverAnswer: At the two ends (poles).

items.prompt_en: Predict: a bar magnet is snapped into two halves. If you bring the broken ends back towards each other, the same way they were joined, will they attract or repel?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek bar magnet do tukdon mein toot jaata hai. Toote hue siron ko waise hi wapas paas laao jaise jude the, toh woh kheenchenge ya dhakelenge?
items.answer: They attract, because new opposite poles form at the break; each half is a complete magnet.
hints: Ask what poles each half must have
Point to the faces at the break
Prompt: at the break, a new N faces a new ___
Assert: they attract; each half has both poles

verified.solverAnswer: Attract.
verified.note: Agrees. Safety advisory: real magnets are brittle and snapping one throws sharp shards; keep strictly a thought experiment (say 'imagine', not 'snapped').

items.prompt_en: Predict: two ring magnets are slid onto a pencil held upright, with like poles facing each other. What will the top magnet do?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: do ring magnet ek khadi pencil mein daale gaye, ek jaise poles aamne-saamne. Upar wala magnet kya karega?
items.answer: It floats (hovers) above the lower magnet, because like poles repel.
hints: Ask what like poles do
Point to gravity pulling the top magnet down
Prompt: the push from like poles holds it ___
Assert: it floats; repulsion balances its weight

verified.solverAnswer: It floats/levitates above (repelled).

items.prompt_en: You saw the top ring magnet float. Why doesn't it fall down onto the lower one?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne dekha upar wala ring magnet tair raha tha. Woh neeche wale pe gir kyon nahi jaata?
items.answer: Like poles face each other and repel; the upward push balances the magnet's weight.
hints: Ask which poles are facing
Point to the force upward and the weight downward
Prompt: repulsion pushes ___ while weight pulls ___
Assert: like-pole repulsion balances its weight

verified.solverAnswer: Like poles repel pushing it up, balancing gravity.

items.prompt_en: An iron nail and a bar magnet are both pulled by your magnet. What test can show which one is the magnet?
items.prompt_hi: Lohe ki keel aur ek bar magnet, dono tumhare magnet se kheenche jaate hain. Kaunsa test batayega ki inme magnet kaunsa hai?
items.answer: The repulsion test: bring each end near one pole of your magnet; if an end is pushed away, that object is a magnet. The iron nail is only ever attracted.
hints: Ask what an iron nail can never do to a magnet
Point to pushing away
Prompt: only a magnet can ___ another magnet
Assert: repulsion is the sure test

verified.solverAnswer: Bring each near a magnet pole/suspended; the one that repels is a magnet; or hang it freely, magnet settles N-S.

items.prompt_en: You have a tiny magnet from a toy kit and a large black fridge magnet. How would you find out which is stronger?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare paas toy kit ka ek chhota magnet aur fridge ka ek bada kaala magnet hai. Kaise pata karoge kaun zyada taakatwar hai?
items.answer: Compare what each can do with the same paper clips: count how many each lifts, or how far away each can pull a clip; don't judge by size.
hints: Ask what would be a fair way to compare
Point to using the same clips
Prompt: count how many ___ each can lift
Assert: test with identical clips; size isn't strength

verified.solverAnswer: Compare how many pins/clips each picks up, or distance at which it attracts.

items.prompt_en: In a magnetic toy train, each carriage joins the next using magnets at its ends. One carriage refuses to join and pushes away. What is happening, and how can you fix it?
items.prompt_hi: Magnetic toy train mein har dibba agle se magnet ke zariye judta hai. Ek dibba judne ki jagah door dhakelta hai. Kya ho raha hai, aur kaise theek karoge?
items.answer: Like poles are facing each other and repelling; turn the carriage around so unlike poles face each other and attract.
hints: Ask what makes magnets push apart
Point to turning the carriage
Prompt: the facing poles are ___; turn it so they are ___
Assert: like poles repel; reverse the carriage

verified.solverAnswer: Like poles facing, so flip the carriage around.

items.prompt_en: Draw two bar magnets for each case and add arrows showing push or pull: (a) N facing S, (b) S facing S.
items.prompt_hi: Har case ke liye do bar magnet banao aur teer se dikhao kheenchna ya dhakelna: (a) N ke saamne S, (b) S ke saamne S.
items.answer: (a) Arrows pointing towards each other: attraction. (b) Arrows pointing away from each other: repulsion.
hints: Invite them to label the poles first
Point to like versus unlike
Prompt: N-S arrows point ___; S-S arrows point ___
Assert: (a) attract, (b) repel

verified.solverAnswer: (a) arrows pulling together; (b) arrows pushing apart.

items.prompt_en: Golu says: 'If I cut my magnet in half, I'll get a north-only magnet and a south-only magnet.' What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Agar main magnet ko beech se kaat doon, toh ek sirf-north aur ek sirf-south magnet milega.' Galti kya hai?
items.answer: Each piece has both a north and a south pole; magnetic poles always come in pairs.

hints: Ask what the broken halves did when brought together
Point to the new poles at the cut
Prompt: every piece has a ___ and a ___ pole
Assert: poles always come in pairs

verified.solverAnswer: Each half gets both N and S poles; poles cannot be separated.

items.prompt_en: Teach your friend the 'rules' of magnets: poles, attraction and repulsion, and how to look after magnets.
items.prompt_hi: Apne dost ko magnet ke 'niyam' sikhao: poles, kheenchna aur dhakelna, aur magnet ki dekhbhaal kaise karein.
items.answer: Key ideas: every magnet has N and S poles, strongest at the ends; like poles repel, unlike attract; repulsion is the sure test; breaking a magnet makes new poles; strength isn't size; heating, hammering or dropping weakens magnets, so store them in pairs with keepers.
hints: Invite them to start with the two poles
Point to the push-pull rule
Prompt: like ___, unlike ___; store magnets in ___
Assert: poles, attraction-repulsion rule, sure test, care

verified.solverAnswer: Two poles N and S; unlike attract, like repel; keep away from heat, dropping, keepers, away from phones/cards.

items.prompt_en: From last time: what is the sure test to know that an object is a magnet?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: kisi cheez ke magnet hone ka pakka test kya hai?
items.answer: Repulsion: if it pushes away a pole of a known magnet, it is a magnet.
hints: Ask what the iron nail could never do
Point to push versus pull
Prompt: the sure test is ___
Assert: repulsion

verified.solverAnswer: Repulsion; if it repels another magnet it is a magnet.

skills.title: State that a freely suspended magnet settles roughly north-south, with its north pole pointing north
Use a compass to find directions
Make a simple compass and explain why it works (the Earth behaves like a giant magnet)

expectations: A freely suspended bar magnet always comes to rest pointing roughly north-south; the end pointing north is its north (north-seeking) pole.
A compass has a small magnetised needle that turns freely; once it settles, turn the compass so the dial's N lines up with the needle's north end, then read the other directions.
The magnet points north because the Earth itself behaves like a giant magnet, not because the north is cold.
Keep a compass away from magnets and iron or steel objects, which disturb the needle.
A simple compass can be made by stroking a steel pin or straightened paper clip many times in one direction with one pole of a magnet and floating it on a piece of cork or a leaf in a bowl of water.

misconceptions.belief: A compass needle points north because it is cold there.
signs: Says 'north mein thand hai'
Thinks a compass would point to a freezer

diagnostic.prompt_en: Why does a compass needle point north?

Because the Earth behaves like a giant magnet and the needle lines up with it
Because the Sun is in the north

items.prompt_en: A bar magnet hangs freely from a thread. When it stops moving, in which directions do its ends point?

items.answer: North and south (roughly); its north pole points north.

Point to the north-seeking end
Prompt: it settles pointing ___ and ___
Assert: roughly north-south, N pole to the north

verified.solverAnswer: North-south: one end points north, the other south.

items.prompt_en: Your compass needle has settled. How do you find east?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare compass ki suyi ruk gayi hai. East (poorab) kaise pata karoge?
items.answer: Turn the compass so the N on the dial lines up with the needle's north end; east is then marked E, a quarter turn clockwise from north (to your right if you face north).

E to the right of N
hints: Ask what has to line up first
Point to the letters on the dial
Prompt: match the dial's ___ with the needle, then read ___
Assert: align N, then E is a quarter turn clockwise

verified.solverAnswer: Face north (needle end): east is on your right.

items.prompt_en: Predict: you hang a bar magnet from a thread, gently turn it to point east-west, and let go. What will happen?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: bar magnet ko dhaage se latka ke halke se east-west mein ghumaao aur chhod do. Kya hoga?
items.answer: It swings and settles back into the north-south direction.
hints: Ask what it did the first time it was hung
Point to the direction it 'wants'
Prompt: it will swing back to ___
Assert: it returns to north-south

verified.solverAnswer: It swings back and settles pointing north-south again.

items.prompt_en: Predict: you stroke a straightened steel paper clip about 30 times in one direction with one pole of a magnet, then float it on a piece of cork in a bowl of water. What will the clip do?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: seedhi ki hui steel ki paper clip ko magnet ke ek pole se ek hi disha mein 30 baar ragdo, phir use cork ke tukde pe rakh ke paani ki katori mein tairao. Clip kya karegi?
items.answer: It turns and settles pointing north-south like a compass, because stroking made it a magnet.
hints: Ask what stroking with a magnet does to steel
Point to the floating cork letting it turn
Prompt: the clip becomes a ___, so it points ___
Assert: it becomes a magnet and settles north-south

verified.solverAnswer: It becomes a magnet and turns to point north-south on the floating cork.

items.prompt_en: Predict: you slowly bring a bar magnet close to a compass lying on the table. What happens to the needle?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: mez pe rakhe compass ke paas dheere-dheere bar magnet laao. Suyi ka kya hoga?
items.answer: The needle swings away from north and turns towards the magnet (its north end is pulled by the magnet's south pole and pushed by its north pole); magnets disturb a compass.
hints: Ask what the needle itself is
Point to the new magnet nearby
Prompt: a nearby magnet ___ the needle
Assert: the needle turns towards the magnet; readings go wrong

verified.solverAnswer: The needle deflects/turns toward the magnet (it points to the magnet's pole rather than north).

items.prompt_en: You said the floating paper clip points north-south. Why does it do that?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne kaha tairti hui paper clip uttar-dakshin mein rukti hai. Woh aisa kyon karti hai?
items.answer: Stroking turned it into a magnet, and since the Earth behaves like a giant magnet, the clip magnet lines up north-south.
acceptable: Earth is like a giant magnet
hints: Ask what the clip became
Point to the Earth as a magnet
Prompt: the Earth acts like a giant ___
Assert: the clip magnet lines up with Earth's magnetism

verified.solverAnswer: It has become a magnet and Earth acts like a giant magnet, so it aligns north-south.

items.prompt_en: Compare a compass placed on a wooden table and one placed on top of a steel almirah. Which reading can you trust, and why?
items.prompt_hi: Lakdi ki mez pe rakha compass aur steel ki almari ke upar rakha compass compare karo. Kis reading pe bharosa kar sakte ho, aur kyon?
items.answer: The one on the wooden table; the iron or steel in the almirah can pull on the needle and give a wrong reading.
