Point to iron disturbing needles
Prompt: steel can pull the ___
Assert: trust the wooden table reading

verified.solverAnswer: Wooden table reading trustworthy; steel almirah (iron) disturbs the needle.

items.prompt_en: Your group must find which wall of a new classroom faces east, using a compass. What steps will you follow?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare group ko compass se pata karna hai ki nayi class ki kaunsi deewar east ki taraf hai. Kaun se steps loge?
items.answer: Hold the compass flat, away from iron and magnets; let the needle settle; turn the compass so N lines up with the needle's north end; look in the direction marked E; the wall in that direction faces east.
hints: Ask what to keep the compass away from
Point to lining up N
Prompt: settle, align ___, then follow ___
Assert: flat, away from iron, align N, read E

verified.solverAnswer: Move away from iron/magnets, let needle settle, face north then east is right; find the wall facing that.

items.prompt_en: Long ago, sailors far out at sea, with clouds hiding the Sun and the stars, still found their direction. How?
items.prompt_hi: Bahut pehle naavik samundar ke beech mein, jab baadal Suraj aur taaron ko chhupa dete the, tab bhi disha dhundh lete the. Kaise?
items.answer: They used a magnetic compass (a magnetised needle or lodestone), which points north-south in any weather.
hints: Ask what works even when you can't see the sky
Point to the magnetised needle
Prompt: a ___ points north-south even in clouds
Assert: a magnetic compass

verified.solverAnswer: Used a magnetic compass (floating lodestone/needle).

items.prompt_en: Draw a compass face and mark N, E, S and W. If you face north, which direction is on your right?
items.prompt_hi: Compass ka chehra banao aur N, E, S, W likho. Agar tum north ki taraf mooh karo, toh tumhare right haath pe kaunsi disha hogi?

hints: Invite them to place N at the top first
Point to going clockwise
Prompt: N, then clockwise ___, S, W
Assert: facing north, east is on the right

items.prompt_en: Golu says: 'A compass needle points north because it is so cold at the North Pole, and magnets like cold.' What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Compass ki suyi north isliye dikhati hai kyonki North Pole pe bahut thand hai, aur magnet ko thand pasand hai.' Galti kya hai?
items.answer: Cold has nothing to do with it; the Earth behaves like a giant magnet, and the needle lines up with it.

Point to the Earth as a magnet

Assert: Earth's magnetism, not cold, sets the direction

verified.solverAnswer: Needle points north because Earth acts like a giant magnet, not cold.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a younger child how to make a pin-and-water compass and why it works.
items.prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko samjhao ki pin aur paani wala compass kaise banate hain aur woh kaam kyon karta hai.
items.answer: Key ideas: stroke a steel pin or straightened paper clip many times in one direction with one pole of a magnet (an adult helps with anything sharp); float it on cork or a leaf in water; it turns north-south because it became a magnet and lines up with the Earth's magnetism; keep it away from other magnets and iron.
hints: Invite them to list the materials first

Prompt: stroking makes it a ___; floating lets it ___
Assert: magnetise, float, it lines up north-south

items.prompt_en: From last time: the end of a freely hanging magnet that points north is called its ___ pole.

Assert: the north pole

skills.title: Explain why standard units are needed, and use the metre with cm, mm and km

expectations: Body measures like a handspan, cubit or foot length differ from person to person, so results differ; standard units give the same result for everyone.
The SI unit of length is the metre (m); 1 m = 100 cm, 1 cm = 10 mm, 1 km = 1000 m.
Place the scale along the length, touching the object, with one end at the zero mark; if the zero is broken or worn, start from another full mark (like 1 cm) and subtract.
Keep your eye directly above the point being read, not at an angle.
A measurement has a number and a unit (e.g. 15.2 cm); 1 metre is about 3.3 feet, so a metre and a foot are not the same.

items.prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Hamara darwaza 2 metre ooncha hai, yaani 2 foot.' Galti kya hai?

skills.title: Use a reference point to decide whether something is at rest or in motion
Classify motion as linear, circular or oscillatory
Recognise objects that show more than one type of motion at once

expectations: An object is in motion if its position changes with time compared with a reference point; it is at rest if its position does not change.
The same object can be at rest relative to one thing and moving relative to another: a passenger is at rest relative to the train seat but moving relative to the platform.
Linear motion is along a straight line (a train on a straight track, a ball dropped straight down).
Circular motion is along a circular path (a seat on a giant wheel, the tip of a fan blade).
Oscillatory motion is to and fro about a central position (a swing, a pendulum, a plucked string).
Some objects show more than one type of motion at once (a rolling bicycle wheel turns round while the bicycle moves straight ahead).

misconceptions.belief: An object is simply moving or not moving; no reference point is needed.
signs: Insists a seated train passenger is 'not moving at all'
Cannot say 'moving compared with what'

items.prompt_en: At a mela, describe the motion of (a) a boat ride that swings to and fro, (b) a merry-go-round, (c) a toy train going straight. Which ride shows two types of motion if its horses also move up and down?
items.prompt_hi: Mele mein in sab ki gati batao: (a) aage-peechhe jhoolti naav, (b) merry-go-round, (c) seedhi chalti toy train. Agar merry-go-round ke ghode upar-neeche bhi hote hain, toh kis ride mein do tarah ki gati hai?
items.answer: (a) Oscillatory, (b) circular, (c) linear. The merry-go-round: its horses go round (circular) and up and down (oscillatory) at the same time.
hints: Ask them to describe the horses' path
Point to round and up-down together
Prompt: the horses go ___ and also ___
Assert: boat oscillatory, merry-go-round circular, train linear; horses show two

verified.solverAnswer: (a) oscillatory (b) circular (c) linear; merry-go-round with up-down horses: circular and oscillatory.

items.prompt_en: Draw arrows to show the path of linear, circular and oscillatory motion. Describe each drawing in words.
items.prompt_hi: Linear, circular aur oscillatory gati ka raasta teer se banao. Har drawing ko shabdon mein batao.
items.answer: Linear: a straight arrow. Circular: an arrow going round a circle. Oscillatory: a two-headed arrow or short arc showing to and fro about a middle point.
hints: Invite them to draw the straight one first
Point to the middle point for oscillation
Prompt: to and fro is shown with a ___-headed arrow
Assert: straight, round, back-and-forth

verified.solverAnswer: Linear straight arrow; circular arrow around a circle; oscillatory arrow back and forth.

items.prompt_en: Golu says: 'A tree is never moving and a running dog is always moving. We don't need a reference point.' What is the problem?
items.prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Ped kabhi nahi chalta aur daudta kutta hamesha chalta hai. Reference point ki zaroorat nahi.' Dikkat kya hai?
items.answer: Whether something is moving depends on what we compare it with: seen from a moving bus, the tree seems to move backwards, and a dog running alongside the bus can stay level with a passenger. We always describe motion with respect to a reference point.
acceptable: from a bus the tree seems to move
hints: Ask how a roadside tree looks from a moving bus
Point to choosing a reference
Prompt: motion always means moving compared with ___
Assert: motion is relative to a reference point

verified.solverAnswer: Motion is relative; tree moves relative to a passing train; need reference.

items.prompt_en: Explain to your cousin the three types of motion using things in a park, and what a reference point is.
items.prompt_hi: Apne cousin ko park ki cheezon se teeno tarah ki gati samjhao, aur reference point kya hota hai.
items.answer: Key ideas: linear (a straight slide), circular (a merry-go-round), oscillatory (a swing); a reference point is a fixed object we compare position with, and whether something is moving depends on it.
hints: Invite them to pick one park ride per type

Prompt: slide ___, merry-go-round ___, swing ___
Assert: three types plus the reference-point idea

verified.solverAnswer: Linear: slide; circular: roundabout; oscillatory: swing; reference point: fixed object.

items.prompt_en: From last time: what type of motion does the pendulum of a wall clock show?

items.answer: Oscillatory motion.

Point to its back-and-forth
Prompt: to and fro is ___
Assert: oscillatory

verified.solverAnswer: Oscillatory.

skills.title: Test and describe lustre, hardness and transparency
Test solubility in water and whether objects float or sink
Recognise that look-alike materials can have different properties, so we test

expectations: Materials have properties we can observe and test: appearance and lustre (shine), hardness, transparency, solubility in water, and whether they float or sink.

Transparent materials let us see through clearly (glass, clean water); translucent ones let some light through but not clearly (butter paper, frosted glass); opaque ones let no light through (wood, cardboard, metal).
Some materials dissolve in water (sugar, salt); others don't (sand, chalk powder, oil).
Whether an object floats or sinks depends on its material and its shape, not just its weight: a big log floats and a small iron nail sinks.
Materials that look alike can have different properties (sugar dissolves, white sand doesn't), so we test instead of guessing.

misconceptions.belief: Materials that look alike have the same properties.

Expects white sand to dissolve like sugar

verified.solverAnswer: Transparent: clear glass, clean water; translucent: butter paper, frosted glass; opaque: wooden board, steel plate.

items.prompt_en: What is lustre? Name two materials that have it.
items.prompt_hi: Lustre kya hai? Do materials batao jinme ye hota hai.
items.answer: Lustre is the shine on a surface; metals such as copper, steel, gold, silver and aluminium have it, especially when freshly polished or cut.

Point to polished metals
Prompt: lustre means ___
Assert: shine; metals like copper and steel

verified.solverAnswer: Lustre is shininess of materials; e.g. gold, silver, steel.

items.prompt_en: Predict which of these will dissolve in water: salt, sand, sugar, chalk powder, a few drops of cooking oil.

items.answer: Salt and sugar dissolve; sand and chalk powder settle at the bottom; the oil floats as a separate layer and doesn't dissolve.

Point to the oil floating in dal
Prompt: ___ and ___ dissolve; oil ___
Assert: salt and sugar dissolve; sand, chalk and oil don't

verified.solverAnswer: Salt and sugar dissolve; sand, chalk powder, oil do not.

items.prompt_en: Predict which of these float and which sink in a bucket of water: a big wooden log, a small iron nail, a hollow plastic ball, a stone.
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo baalti ke paani mein kaun tairega aur kaun doobega: bada lakdi ka latha, chhoti lohe ki keel, khokhli plastic ki ball, ek patthar.
items.answer: The log and the plastic ball float; the nail and the stone sink.
hints: Ask whether the heaviest thing here is the log
Point to what each is made of
Prompt: wood and hollow plastic ___; iron and stone ___
Assert: log and ball float; nail and stone sink

verified.solverAnswer: Log floats, hollow ball floats; nail and stone sink.

items.prompt_en: Predict: you place an empty steel katori gently, right side up, on the water in a bucket. Will it float or sink? What if it fills with water?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: khaali steel ki katori ko seedha baalti ke paani pe halke se rakho. Tairegi ya doobegi? Aur agar usme paani bhar jaaye toh?
items.answer: The empty katori floats because of its hollow shape; if it fills with water it sinks. Shape matters, not just the material.
hints: Ask how a heavy steel ship floats
Point to the air-filled hollow
Prompt: the hollow shape helps it ___; full of water, it ___
Assert: floats when empty, sinks when full

verified.solverAnswer: Empty katori floats; when it fills with water it sinks.

items.prompt_en: You said the heavy log floats but the light nail sinks. Why?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne kaha bhaari latha tairta hai aur halki keel doobti hai. Kyon?
items.answer: Floating depends on the material and shape, not on total weight: wood is light for its size compared with water, while iron is heavy for its size, so the nail sinks.
hints: Ask what each is made of
Point to 'for its size'
Prompt: wood is ___ for its size; iron is ___ for its size
Assert: material and shape decide, not total weight

verified.solverAnswer: Floating depends on the material (density) not weight; wood is less dense than water, iron is denser.

items.prompt_en: A clear plastic tumbler and a glass tumbler look the same. Name one property that differs and how you could test it safely.
items.prompt_hi: Plastic ka saaf tumbler aur kaanch ka tumbler ek jaise dikhte hain. Ek property batao jo alag hai aur use safely kaise test karoge.
items.answer: For example, flexibility: press gently and the plastic bends a little while the glass stays rigid; the glass would break if dropped, so don't test by dropping. Tapping also gives a different sound.
hints: Ask what happens when each is squeezed gently
Point to never dropping glass to test
Prompt: plastic ___ when pressed; glass ___
Assert: plastic flexes, glass is rigid and breaks

verified.solverAnswer: Hardness or breakability; plastic can bend/less brittle; tapping or dropping from low height on soft surface; weight.

Point to light versus seeing through
Prompt: frosted glass lets ___ through but not a clear ___

items.prompt_en: Fishing nets have floats tied along the top edge and weights along the bottom. What might the floats and weights be made of, and why?
items.prompt_hi: Machhli pakadne ke jaal mein upar ke kinare pe float aur neeche ke kinare pe vazan bandhe hote hain. Float aur vazan kis cheez ke ho sakte hain, aur kyon?
items.answer: Floats: materials that float, such as plastic, thermocol or wood. Weights: materials that sink, such as lead, iron or stones. Together they hold the net upright like a wall in the water.
hints: Ask what keeps the top of the net up

items.prompt_hi: Ek table banao jisme columns hon: chamakdaar?, sakht?, ghulta hai?, tairta hai? aur steel ki chammach, lakdi ki chammach aur mom ke tukde ke liye bharo.
items.answer: Steel spoon: shiny ✓, hard ✓, dissolves ✗, floats ✗. Wooden spoon: shiny ✗, hard ✓, dissolves ✗, floats ✓. Wax: shiny ✗, hard ✗ (a fingernail scratches it), dissolves ✗, floats ✓.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a friend five properties we can test in materials, with one quick home test for each.
items.prompt_hi: Ek dost ko paanch properties samjhao jo hum materials mein test kar sakte hain, aur har ek ka ghar pe karne wala ek chhota test.
items.answer: Key ideas: lustre (look for shine); hardness (press or scratch gently with a fingernail); transparency (hold it up to a light); solubility (stir a little into water); floating or sinking (put it in a bucket of water).

Assert: five properties, each with a safe home test

skills.title: Tell an object apart from the material it is made of
Group materials by a chosen property
Relate the properties of materials to their uses

expectations: An object is a thing (spoon, chair, bag); a material is what it is made of (steel, wood, plastic, cloth).
The same object can be made from different materials, and the same material can make many different objects.
We group materials by properties, such as hard or soft, transparent or opaque, floats or sinks, or whether heat passes through them easily.

Uses depend on properties: cooking pans are metal because heat passes through metal quickly and it doesn't melt on the stove; handles are plastic or wood because heat doesn't pass through them easily, so they stay cool to hold.
Choosing a material means matching its properties to what the job needs.

skills.title: Explain why touch is not a reliable way to judge how hot something is
Use temperature in degrees Celsius as the measure of how hot or cold something is
Tell heat apart from temperature and explain why metal feels colder than wood

expectations: Touch can mislead: after a hand is in cold water, lukewarm water feels warm; after warm water, the same lukewarm water feels cool.
Temperature is a measure of how hot or cold something is, measured with a thermometer, usually in degrees Celsius (°C).
At room temperature a steel spoon and a wooden spoon are at the same temperature; metal feels colder because it takes heat away from your hand faster.

Heat is energy that flows from a hotter object to a colder one; temperature tells how hot something is. They are not the same: a bucket of warm water has more heat than a cup of hot chai, but a lower temperature.
Water freezes at 0 °C and boils at about 100 °C; normal human body temperature is about 37 °C.

items.prompt_en: You said the steel and the wood are at the same temperature. Why does the steel feel colder, then?

items.prompt_en: Compare a cup of hot chai and a bucket of warm bathwater. Which has the higher temperature? Which holds more heat?

items.prompt_en: Why do we wear woollen sweaters in winter? Do sweaters make heat?

Point to the body as the heat source

Assert: wool slows heat loss by trapping air

items.prompt_en: Golu says: 'Heat and temperature are the same. A big bucket of warm water has a higher temperature than a small cup of hot chai, because it has more heat.' What is wrong?

skills.title: Know the range and use of clinical (about 35-42 °C) and laboratory (about −10 to 110 °C) thermometers
Read a thermometer scale by finding the value of the smallest division
Use clinical and laboratory thermometers safely and correctly

expectations: A clinical thermometer measures body temperature; its range is about 35 °C to 42 °C because body temperature stays within this range.
A laboratory thermometer has a wider range, usually −10 °C to 110 °C, for measuring other things, such as water.
Normal human body temperature is about 37 °C (98.6 °F); it varies a little from person to person.
To read a scale, find the value of one small division (often 0.1 °C on a clinical thermometer and 1 °C on a lab thermometer) and count.
Lab thermometer: keep it upright, with the bulb in the liquid but not touching the bottom or sides, and read it while it is still in the liquid, with your eye level with the top of the column.

Digital thermometers are safer than mercury ones; mercury is poisonous, so a broken mercury thermometer is cleaned up only by an adult. Never use a clinical thermometer for very hot things like boiling water.

items.prompt_en: You said to read the lab thermometer while it's still in the water. Why?

items.prompt_en: Compare a clinical thermometer and a laboratory thermometer: range, use and one special feature.

items.answer: Clinical: about 35-42 °C, for body temperature; a mercury one has a kink so the reading stays until shaken, and digital ones beep when done. Lab: about −10 to 110 °C, for liquids and experiments; no kink, so it must be read while in the liquid.
hints: Ask what each one is used to measure
Point to the range on each
Prompt: clinical is for ___; lab is for ___
Assert: different ranges, uses and reading rules

items.prompt_en: A digital thermometer shows 101.3 °F for your sister. Normal is about 98.6 °F. Does she have a fever?

items.prompt_en: Golu wants to check if the chai is too hot by dipping the family's clinical thermometer in it. What is the problem, and what should be used instead?
items.prompt_hi: Golu ghar ke clinical thermometer ko chai mein daal ke dekhna chahta hai ki chai zyada garam hai ya nahi. Dikkat kya hai, aur iski jagah kya use karna chahiye?

items.prompt_en: Teach your cousin how to take someone's temperature correctly with a clinical thermometer.

items.answer: Key ideas: clean it; for a mercury type, shake it until it reads below 35 °C; place it under the tongue or in the armpit; wait about a minute (or until a digital one beeps); read it holding it at eye level; clean it again; normal is about 37 °C.

skills.title: Describe ice, water and water vapour by their shape and how they fill space

expectations: Water exists as a solid (ice, with a fixed shape), a liquid (water, which takes the shape of its container but keeps its amount) and a gas (water vapour, which is invisible and spreads to fill any space).
Ice melts into water at 0 °C, and water freezes into ice at 0 °C; water boils at about 100 °C and turns into vapour; vapour condenses back into water when it cools.
Water vapour is invisible; the white 'steam' cloud above boiling water or a pressure cooker is made of tiny droplets of condensed water.
The big bubbles that rise in boiling water are water vapour, not air (the tiny bubbles seen when water first warms are dissolved air coming out).
Melting (ice turning into water when warmed) is different from dissolving (sugar spreading into water to make a solution).
Water expands when it freezes, so ice is lighter than the same volume of water and floats.

items.prompt_en: Predict: an ice cube in a glass and a spoon of sugar stirred into a glass of water both 'disappear'. Is it the same kind of change?

items.prompt_en: Predict: you fill an ice tray right to the top with water and freeze it. Will the ice be level with the top, below it, or bulging above it?

items.prompt_en: Why does an ice cube float in a glass of water?

Assert: floating ice shields the liquid water below

items.prompt_en: Draw ice, water and water vapour at the corners of a triangle. Label each arrow between them with the name of the change.

items.prompt_en: Golu says: 'When water boils, the bubbles are air going in, and the white steam I see is water vapour.' Find both mistakes.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a younger child the difference between melting and dissolving, using ice and sugar.

skills.title: Explain evaporation as water turning into vapour from the surface at any temperature
Explain condensation as vapour cooling into droplets on a cool surface
Use evaporation and condensation to explain everyday events and the water cycle

expectations: Evaporation is liquid water turning into water vapour; it happens slowly at all temperatures from the water's surface, not only when water boils.
Clothes dry, puddles disappear and wet floors dry because the water evaporates into the air; the water is not destroyed.
Condensation is water vapour in the air cooling and turning into tiny water droplets on a cool surface (drops outside a cold glass, dew on grass, mist on a bathroom mirror).
The drops on the outside of a cold glass come from the air around it, not through the glass.
Evaporation and condensation drive the water cycle: water evaporates from seas, lakes and plants, condenses into clouds and falls as rain.

items.prompt_en: What is evaporation? Give two examples from home.

items.prompt_en: Explain how water from the Bay of Bengal can end up as rain on a farm in Odisha.

skills.title: Name the factors that speed up evaporation: temperature, wind, surface area, dry air

expectations: Evaporation is faster when it is hotter, when there is wind, when the water is spread over a larger surface and when the air is dry (less humid).
To test one factor fairly, change only that factor and keep the amount of water and everything else the same.
Evaporation takes heat from the surface it happens from, so it cools that surface: sweat drying cools the body, and a wet cloth cools the forehead.
A matka cools water because water seeps through its tiny pores and evaporates from the outside surface, taking heat from the pot and the water inside; the clay itself is not 'cold'.
In humid weather evaporation is slow, so sweat doesn't dry and a matka cools less; a fan cools us by speeding up the evaporation of sweat, not by making the air colder.

skills.title: Explain why we separate mixtures

expectations: We separate mixtures to remove unwanted or harmful parts or to get the useful parts.
Handpicking: picking out by hand pieces that differ in size, colour or shape (stones from dal or rice).
Threshing: beating or crushing harvested stalks to separate the grain from the stalks.
Winnowing: letting a mixture fall from a height in the wind so the lighter husk blows away and the heavier grain falls nearby.
Sieving: using a sieve to separate particles of different sizes (bran from flour, pebbles from sand).

skills.title: Use sedimentation and decantation for heavy insoluble solids
Use filtration to remove insoluble solids from a liquid

expectations: Sedimentation: heavier insoluble particles settle to the bottom when a mixture is left undisturbed. Decantation: gently pouring off the clearer liquid above the settled layer.
Filtration: passing a mixture through a filter (filter paper, cloth, tea strainer) traps insoluble solids and lets the liquid through.
Dissolved substances like salt or sugar pass through a filter, so filtration can't remove them.
Dissolved salt has not disappeared: when salt water is left in the sun, the water evaporates and the salt is left behind, as in the salt pans of the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat.
Clear-looking water is not necessarily safe to drink; germs and dissolved substances can remain, so it needs boiling or purifying.

skills.title: List the features of living things: need food, grow, respire, respond, get rid of wastes, reproduce, have a life span
Decide whether something is living by checking all the features together, not just one
Recognise plants and seeds as living things

expectations: Living things need food, grow, respire (take in air to get energy from food), respond to changes around them, get rid of wastes, reproduce, and have a life span after which they die.
Something is living only if it shows these features together; one feature, like moving, is not enough.
Some non-living things move (a car, a cloud, a river) or seem to grow (a flame, a crystal), but they don't grow by building their own body from food, respire, or produce young ones of their kind.
Plants are living: they grow, make and use food, respire, respond (touch-me-not leaves fold, shoots bend towards light) and reproduce.
Seeds are living but resting (dormant); given water, air and warmth they germinate.

misconceptions.belief: Anything that moves, such as a car, fire or a cloud, is alive.
signs: Says a car is alive because it moves and 'eats' petrol
Says clouds or rivers are alive

diagnostic.prompt_en: A car moves and uses petrol. Is it living?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Car chalti hai aur petrol use karti hai. Kya woh jeevit hai?

options.text: Yes, it moves and eats petrol, so it's alive
No; it doesn't grow, reproduce or respond on its own like living things
Only while it is running

remediation.representation: Living checklist card with seven boxes, filled in for a puppy and a car

misconceptions.belief: Plants and seeds are not alive because they don't walk or eat like animals.

Says dry seeds are dead

diagnostic.prompt_en: Is a dry moong seed in your kitchen jar living?

options.text: No, it doesn't move or eat
Yes; it is living but resting, and with water, air and warmth it will sprout
It becomes alive only after cooking

remediation.representation: Sprouting time-lapse: dry seed → swollen seed → sprout
remediation.moveShape: Child starts sprouting a few moong seeds and logs the change each day as evidence of life

misconceptions.belief: Plants don't respire, or respire only at night, because they have no nose or lungs.
signs: Says plants don't breathe
Says only animals with lungs respire

diagnostic.prompt_en: Do plants respire?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kya paudhe shwasan (respiration) karte hain?

options.text: No, they have no nose or lungs
Yes; all living things respire, and plants take in air through tiny pores in their leaves and other parts
Only at night

remediation.representation: Leaf close-up showing tiny pores with air arrows, day and night panels
remediation.moveShape: Ask what all living things need energy for; connect energy to respiration in every cell, day and night

items.prompt_en: List five features that all living things show.
items.prompt_hi: Paanch khoobiyan batao jo saare jeevit cheezon mein hoti hain.
items.answer: Any five: need food, grow, respire, respond to changes around them, get rid of wastes, reproduce, have a life span and die.
hints: Ask what a puppy does that a toy doesn't
Point to growing and having babies
Prompt: living things grow, need ___, ___ and reproduce
Assert: food, growth, respiration, response, waste removal, reproduction, life span

verified.solverAnswer: Need food, respire, grow, respond to surroundings, reproduce, excrete (move, die).

items.prompt_en: Sort these into living and non-living: a cow, a bicycle, a mango tree, a cloud, a mushroom, a stone.
items.prompt_hi: Inhe jeevit aur nirjeev mein baanto: gaay, cycle, aam ka ped, baadal, mushroom, patthar.
items.answer: Living: cow, mango tree, mushroom. Non-living: bicycle, cloud, stone.
hints: Ask which ones grow and reproduce
Point to the cloud and the bicycle moving
Prompt: moving alone doesn't make something ___
Assert: cow, tree, mushroom living; the rest non-living

verified.solverAnswer: Living: cow, mango tree, mushroom. Non-living: bicycle, cloud, stone.

items.prompt_en: Predict: you gently touch the leaves of a touch-me-not (chhui-mui, lajwanti) plant. What will happen, and what does it show?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: chhui-mui (lajwanti) ke patton ko halke se chhoo do. Kya hoga, aur isse kya pata chalta hai?
items.answer: The leaflets quickly fold and droop; it shows that plants respond to touch, so they are living.
hints: Ask what the plant's name suggests
Point to response as a feature of life
Prompt: the leaves ___ when touched, so the plant ___
Assert: the leaves fold; plants respond, so they're living

verified.solverAnswer: The leaves fold/droop; shows response to touch.

items.prompt_en: Predict: you keep some dry chana in a dry box and some on wet cotton for three days. What will you see in each?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: kuch sookhe chane sookhe dabbe mein aur kuch geeli rui pe teen din rakho. Dono mein kya dikhega?
items.answer: The chana on wet cotton swell and sprout; the ones in the dry box stay the same. Seeds are alive but resting.
hints: Ask what seeds need to wake up
Point to water as the difference
Prompt: with water, the seeds ___
Assert: wet ones sprout; seeds are alive but dormant

verified.solverAnswer: Dry box: nothing; wet cotton: sprouts.

items.prompt_en: Predict: a potted plant is kept on a windowsill for a week without being turned. Which way will its shoot bend?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: gamle ka paudha ek hafte khidki pe bina ghumaye rakha hai. Uski tehni kis taraf jhukegi?
items.answer: Towards the light (the window); plants respond to light.
hints: Ask where the light comes from
Point to the tulsi example
Prompt: shoots grow towards ___
Assert: it bends towards the light

verified.solverAnswer: Toward the window (light).

items.prompt_en: You said the car is not living even though it moves. How did you decide?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne kaha car chalti hai phir bhi jeevit nahi hai. Ye kaise decide kiya?
items.answer: Living things show all the features together; a car doesn't grow, reproduce, respire like living things or respond on its own, so moving alone isn't enough.
hints: Ask how many checklist boxes the car fills
Point to growth and reproduction
Prompt: living things show ___ the features, not just one
Assert: one feature isn't enough

verified.solverAnswer: Car doesn't grow, reproduce, respire, respond like living things.

items.prompt_en: Compare a growing puppy with a diya flame you have seen. Both 'need air' and can get bigger. What makes only one of them living?
items.prompt_hi: Badhte hue pille aur kabhi dekhi diye ki lau compare karo. Dono ko 'hawa chahiye' aur dono bade ho sakte hain. Kya cheez sirf ek ko jeevit banaati hai?
items.answer: The puppy eats, grows into an adult by building its own body, respires, responds, will reproduce and has a life span. The flame isn't made of cells, doesn't feed and build a body, has no life cycle and doesn't produce young of its kind, so it is non-living.
hints: Ask whether a flame grows up and has babies
Point to the checklist
Prompt: the puppy grows by eating; the flame doesn't have a ___
Assert: only the puppy shows all features

verified.solverAnswer: Puppy grows, reproduces, responds; flame just burns fuel; not alive.

items.prompt_en: Is the mango tree in your colony living? Give three pieces of evidence.
items.prompt_hi: Kya tumhari colony ka aam ka ped jeevit hai? Teen saboot do.
items.answer: Yes. Any three: it grows taller and gets new leaves; it needs water and makes its own food; it respires; it flowers and makes fruits with seeds (reproduces); it responds to light; it will die one day.
hints: Ask what changes on the tree each year
Point to the mango season
Prompt: it grows, makes ___, and needs ___
Assert: growth, food and water, reproduction show it's living

verified.solverAnswer: It grows, makes food, responds to light, reproduces by seeds, respires.

items.prompt_en: Scientists searching for life on Mars look for certain signs. What signs would tell them something is living?
items.prompt_hi: Mangal pe jeevan dhundhne wale vaigyanik kuch nishaaniyan dhundhte hain. Kaunsi nishaaniyan batayengi ki koi cheez jeevit hai?
items.answer: Signs that it takes in food or energy, grows, respires (exchanges gases), gets rid of wastes, responds to changes, and reproduces.
hints: Ask how they'd know a tiny thing is alive
Point to the checklist
Prompt: it would need to grow, use ___ and make ___
Assert: the same life features, together

verified.solverAnswer: Growth, reproduction, respiration/gases exchange, response, need for food/energy.

items.prompt_en: Make a table with the features grows, needs food, respires, responds and reproduces as rows, and a cow, a mango tree and a car as columns. Fill in ✓ or ✗.
items.prompt_hi: Ek table banao: rows mein 'badhta hai, khaana chahiye, shwasan karta hai, pratikriya deta hai, prajanan karta hai', aur columns mein gaay, aam ka ped aur car. ✓ ya ✗ bharo.
items.answer: Cow: ✓ for all five. Mango tree: ✓ for all five. Car: ✗ for all five (fuel is not food, and it doesn't grow, respire, respond on its own or reproduce).
hints: Invite them to fill the cow column first
Point to the car using fuel, not food
Prompt: the tree also ___ and ___
Assert: cow and tree all ✓; car all ✗

verified.solverAnswer: Cow: all ticks. Mango tree: grows, needs food (makes own), respires, responds, reproduces. Car: all crosses.

items.prompt_en: Golu says: 'Plants are non-living because they can't walk, and dry seeds are dead.' What would you tell him?
items.prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Paudhe nirjeev hain kyonki chal nahi sakte, aur sookhe beej mare hue hote hain.' Tum use kya bataoge?
items.answer: Walking from place to place isn't needed: plants grow, respire, respond and reproduce, so they are living; seeds are alive but resting and sprout when given water, air and warmth.
hints: Ask what the chana on wet cotton did
Point to the chhui-mui
Prompt: plants ___ and ___, so they are living
Assert: plants and seeds are living

verified.solverAnswer: Plants are living (grow, respire, reproduce, respond); dry seeds are living but resting.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a younger child how to decide whether something is living, using a seed and a toy car.
items.prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko beej aur khilone wali car ke example se samjhao ki koi cheez jeevit hai ya nahi, kaise decide karein.
items.answer: Key ideas: check all the features together; a seed came from a parent plant, respires slowly, grows into a plant when given water, air and warmth, and that plant makes new seeds, so it is living; a toy car may move but doesn't grow, eat, respire or reproduce, so it is non-living.
hints: Invite them to run the checklist on the seed
Point to the toy car failing most boxes
Prompt: the seed can ___ and make new ___; the car can't
Assert: use all the features together

verified.solverAnswer: Seed grows into plant when given water; toy car doesn't grow, respire, reproduce.

items.prompt_en: From last time: name one way a plant shows that it responds to its surroundings.
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek tareeka batao jisse paudha dikhata hai ki woh aas-paas ke badlaav pe pratikriya deta hai.
items.answer: Any one: touch-me-not leaves fold when touched; shoots bend towards light; roots grow towards water; some flowers open in the day and close at night.
hints: Ask what the windowsill plant did
Point to the touch-me-not
Prompt: shoots bend towards ___
Assert: e.g. bending to light or folding to touch

verified.solverAnswer: Bending toward light; leaves fold on touch; roots grow downward.

skills.title: State the conditions most seeds need to germinate: water, air and suitable warmth
Design a fair test of one germination condition
Explain why soil and light are not needed for germination but are needed later

expectations: Germination is when a seed starts growing into a young plant (sprouting).
Seeds like moong and chana need water, air and suitable warmth to germinate.
They don't need soil or sunlight to germinate, because they use food stored inside them; moong sprouts in a wet cloth even in the dark.
After germination, the young plant needs light to make its own food and soil (or water with nutrients) to keep growing; seedlings kept in the dark grow pale and long.
Seeds kept fully under water for days get too little air and germinate poorly or not at all.
A fair test changes only one condition and keeps the rest the same (same seeds, number, container, place).

misconceptions.belief: Seeds need soil and sunlight to germinate.
signs: Always plans germination tests with soil and sunlight
Is surprised moong sprouts in a dark box

diagnostic.prompt_en: Moong seeds wrapped in a wet cloth are kept inside a dark kitchen box. Will they sprout?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Geele kapde mein lipte moong ke daane rasoi ke andhere dabbe mein rakhe hain. Kya woh ankurit honge?

options.text: No, they need soil and sunlight
Yes; they need water, air and warmth, not soil or light
Only if fertiliser is added

remediation.representation: Seed cut-open diagram showing its stored food
remediation.moveShape: Ask where the first food for the sprout comes from; reveal the stored food; then run the dark-box test

misconceptions.belief: More water is always better, so seeds kept fully under water germinate best.
signs: Drowns seeds in a glass
Says more water means faster sprouting

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which set will germinate best?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kaunsa set sabse achha ankurit hoga?

options.text: Seeds kept fully under water in a glass for many days
Seeds on wet cotton with air around them
Seeds kept dry in a box

remediation.representation: Three-glass setup: dry, wet cotton, fully under water, with sprout counts after 4 days
remediation.moveShape: Child predicts the counts, compares with results and names the missing condition in each failing glass

misconceptions.belief: Germination needs only water; warmth doesn't matter.
signs: Predicts seeds in the fridge will sprout as well as those on the shelf
Ignores winter slow-down

diagnostic.prompt_en: Two sets of seeds on wet cotton: one in the fridge, one at room temperature. What happens?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Geeli rui pe beejon ke do set: ek fridge mein, ek kamre ke temperature pe. Kya hoga?

options.text: Both sprout equally
The room-temperature set sprouts; the cold set sprouts very slowly or not at all
Only the fridge set sprouts

remediation.representation: Temperature strip with sprout counts at fridge, room and warm positions
remediation.moveShape: Child places predicted counts on the strip, then compares with the results

items.prompt_en: What three conditions do seeds need to germinate?
items.prompt_hi: Beejon ko ankurit hone ke liye kaunsi teen cheezein chahiye?
items.answer: Water, air and suitable warmth.

Point to air and warmth too
Prompt: water, ___ and ___
Assert: water, air, warmth

items.prompt_en: You want to test whether seeds need water. Describe the two sets you will make and what stays the same.
items.prompt_hi: Tum test karna chahte ho ki kya beejon ko paani chahiye. Kaunse do set banaoge aur kya same rakhoge?
items.answer: Set A: seeds on dry cotton. Set B: seeds on wet cotton. Keep the same: kind and number of seeds, container, place and warmth; compare after 3-4 days.
hints: Ask what the one difference should be
Point to everything else staying equal
Prompt: only ___ changes; same seeds, place and ___
Assert: dry vs wet, everything else the same

verified.solverAnswer: One set with water, one dry; same seeds, same warmth, same place, only water changes.

items.prompt_en: Predict: moong seeds on wet cotton are kept in a dark cupboard, and another set in a sunny window. Will both sprout?

items.answer: Yes, both sprout; light isn't needed for germination. (Later, the dark ones grow pale and long.)

Point to the stored food inside
Prompt: germination doesn't need ___
Assert: both sprout; light comes in later

verified.solverAnswer: Yes, both sprout (no light needed).

items.prompt_en: Predict: set 1 of seeds stays fully under water for 4 days; set 2 sits on wet cotton. Which sprouts better?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: set 1 ke beej 4 din poore paani mein doobe rehte hain; set 2 geeli rui pe hai. Kaun behtar ankurit hoga?
items.answer: Set 2; seeds kept fully under water get too little air, so they germinate poorly or not at all.
hints: Ask what the drowned seeds are missing
Point to air around the cotton seeds
Prompt: seeds need water and also ___
Assert: wet cotton wins; drowned seeds lack air

verified.solverAnswer: Wet cotton set (water-logged seeds lack air).

items.prompt_en: Predict: seeds on wet cotton are kept in the fridge, and another set on the kitchen shelf, for 3 days. What happens?

Point to warmth as a condition
Prompt: too cold means ___ sprouting

items.prompt_en: You said seeds sprout even in a dark box. Why don't they need sunlight yet?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne kaha beej andhere dabbe mein bhi ankurit hote hain. Unhe abhi dhoop ki zaroorat kyon nahi?
items.answer: The seed has food stored inside it for its first growth; light is needed later, when the leaves start making food.
hints: Ask what is inside a split chana
Point to leaves as the later food-makers
Prompt: the seed uses its own ___ at first
Assert: stored food powers germination

verified.solverAnswer: Seeds have stored food, no need for light until leaves.

items.prompt_en: After a week, seedlings grown in a dark box look pale yellow and long; those grown near a window are green and short. What does this tell you?

Point to the colour difference later
Prompt: germination without light, but growth needs ___
Assert: light matters after sprouting, not for it

verified.solverAnswer: Light is needed for green colour (chlorophyll) and normal growth; in dark they get pale, tall.

items.prompt_en: Why do farmers sow many seeds after the first monsoon rains and not in dry soil?
items.prompt_hi: Kisaan bahut se beej pehli monsoon baarish ke baad kyon bote hain, sookhi mitti mein kyon nahi?
items.answer: Seeds need water to germinate; the rain wets the soil, and it is warm too.

Point to the three conditions
Prompt: rain supplies the ___
Assert: water from the rain lets seeds germinate

items.prompt_en: Your class wants to test whether warmth affects how fast seeds sprout. Plan a fair test with what you have at home, without any heater or flame.

items.answer: Two identical containers with the same number and kind of seeds on equally wet cotton; cover both so the light is the same; keep one in a warm spot in the house and one in the fridge; count sprouted seeds each day and repeat the test.

Point to covering both so light is the same
Prompt: only the ___ differs; count sprouts every ___

items.prompt_en: Riya's sprouting record for 10 seeds on wet cotton: Day 1: 0, Day 2: 3, Day 3: 8, Day 4: 10. Her dry set stayed at 0 every day. Draw a bar or line graph and tell me what it shows.
items.prompt_hi: Riya ka record, geeli rui pe 10 beej: Din 1: 0, Din 2: 3, Din 3: 8, Din 4: 10. Uska sookha set har din 0 raha. Bar ya line graph banao aur batao isse kya pata chalta hai.
items.answer: The wet set rises to 10 by day 4 while the dry set stays at 0; seeds need water to germinate.
hints: Invite them to plot the wet set first
Point to the flat dry line
Prompt: the wet line goes ___; the dry line stays at ___
Assert: water makes the difference

items.prompt_en: Golu tests water: wet seeds in a warm room and dry seeds in the fridge. He says, 'Water is needed.' What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Golu paani ka test karta hai: geele beej garam kamre mein aur sookhe beej fridge mein. Woh kehta hai, 'Paani zaroori hai.' Galti kya hai?

Point to the fridge

Assert: unfair; change only water

items.prompt_en: Explain to your mother why moong sprouts in a wet cloth without soil or sunlight, and why the sprouts must not be left under water.
items.prompt_hi: Mummy ko samjhao ki moong geele kapde mein bina mitti ya dhoop ke kyon ankurit hota hai, aur ankur ko paani mein dooba kar kyon nahi chhodna chahiye.
items.answer: Key ideas: seeds need water, air and warmth; they have stored food, so they don't need soil or light to sprout; kept fully under water they get too little air and sprout poorly.
hints: Invite them to name the three needs
Point to the stored food and the need for air
Prompt: stored food replaces ___ and light; under water there's no ___
Assert: water, air, warmth; no soil or light needed; don't drown them

verified.solverAnswer: Seeds have stored food; need only water, air, warmth; under water they lack air and rot.

items.prompt_en: From last time: does a seed need soil to germinate?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: kya beej ko ankurit hone ke liye mitti chahiye?
items.answer: No; it needs water, air and warmth.
hints: Ask where the moong sprouted
Point to the wet cloth
Prompt: it sprouted without ___
Assert: no soil needed

verified.solverAnswer: No.

skills.title: Put the stages of a flowering plant's life cycle in order
Put the stages of the mosquito's life cycle in order and link them to breeding sites
Put the stages of the frog's life cycle in order and explain metamorphosis

expectations: A life cycle is the series of stages a living thing passes through, from its start to an adult that can reproduce, and then it repeats.
Plant: seed → germination → seedling → adult plant → flowers → fruits with seeds → new plants.
Mosquito: egg → larva → pupa → adult; eggs are laid on still water, and the larvae and pupae live in the water.

Frog: eggs in water → tadpole (gills, tail, lives in water) → tadpole with legs as the tail shrinks → froglet → adult frog (lungs; lives on land and in water). This big change in body form is called metamorphosis.
A tadpole and a frog are the same animal at different stages; emptying still water every week breaks the mosquito's life cycle.

misconceptions.belief: Tadpoles and frogs are different animals.
signs: Says a tadpole is a fish
Is surprised that tadpoles become frogs

diagnostic.prompt_en: What will the tadpoles in a pond become?

options.text: Fish
Frogs
They stay tadpoles forever

In the air

Expects a baby frog to be a tiny frog

No; it hatches as a wriggling larva in water, then becomes a pupa before turning into the adult
It hatches as a flying pupa

items.prompt_en: Put the mosquito's stages in order: adult, egg, pupa, larva.

items.answer: Egg → larva → pupa → adult.

items.prompt_en: Put the frog's stages in order: froglet, eggs, adult frog, tadpole.

items.prompt_en: Put a mango plant's life cycle in order: flowers, seed, fruit, seedling, adult tree.

verified.solverAnswer: Seed, seedling, adult tree, flowers, fruit.

items.prompt_en: Predict: after the rains, water collects in an old tyre and stays there for two weeks. What could you find in it?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: baarish ke baad ek purane tyre mein paani bhar gaya aur do hafte tak raha. Usme kya mil sakta hai?
items.answer: Mosquito larvae and pupae (wrigglers), and soon adult mosquitoes.
hints: Ask where mosquitoes lay eggs
Point to the still water
Prompt: still water for a week or more grows ___
Assert: larvae and pupae, then adult mosquitoes

verified.solverAnswer: Mosquito eggs, wriggling larvae and pupae.

items.prompt_en: Predict: you see a tadpole that has tiny back legs. What will change next over the coming weeks?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek tadpole dikha jiske peechhe chhote pair nikal aaye hain. Agle kuch hafton mein aage kya badlega?
items.answer: Front legs will appear, the tail will shrink away and lungs will develop; it becomes a froglet and then a frog.
hints: Ask which legs come first
Point to the tail
Prompt: next come the ___ legs, and the tail ___
Assert: front legs, tail shrinks, lungs form, froglet, frog

verified.solverAnswer: The back legs grow, front legs appear, tail shrinks, it becomes a froglet.

items.prompt_en: Predict: a family empties and scrubs its cooler and flower-pot trays every week. What happens to the mosquito life cycle there?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek parivaar har hafte cooler aur gamlon ki trays khaali karke ragad ke saaf karta hai. Wahan machhar ke jeevan-chakra ka kya hoga?
items.answer: The eggs and larvae are thrown out before they can become adults (which takes about a week), so mosquitoes can't complete their life cycle there and there are fewer mosquitoes.
hints: Ask how long a mosquito takes from egg to adult
Point to the weekly cleaning
Prompt: emptying before a ___ stops them becoming adults
Assert: weekly emptying breaks the cycle

verified.solverAnswer: Cycle is broken; no larvae develop.

items.prompt_en: You said the tadpole becomes a frog. Why does a tadpole have gills but a frog has lungs?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne kaha tadpole medhak banta hai. Tadpole ke gills aur medhak ke lungs kyon hote hain?
items.answer: The tadpole lives only in water, so it breathes with gills; the adult frog lives on land and in water and breathes air with lungs (and through its moist skin).
hints: Ask where each one lives
Point to the fish's gills
Prompt: in water → ___; in air → ___
Assert: gills for water life, lungs for land life

verified.solverAnswer: Tadpole lives in water breathing through gills; frog on land with lungs (metamorphosis).

items.prompt_en: Compare a tadpole and an adult frog: where they live, how they breathe and how they move.
items.prompt_hi: Tadpole aur adult medhak compare karo: kahan rehte hain, kaise saans lete hain aur kaise chalte hain.
items.answer: Tadpole: lives in water, breathes with gills, swims with its tail. Adult frog: lives on land and in water, breathes with lungs (and its skin), jumps with strong back legs and swims with webbed feet.
hints: Invite them to compare one thing at a time
Point to the tail and the legs
Prompt: tadpole swims with its ___; frog jumps with its ___
Assert: same animal, very different bodies

verified.solverAnswer: Tadpole water, gills, swims with tail; frog land and water, lungs/skin, legs for jumping.

items.prompt_en: Why does the health department ask families to keep a weekly 'dry day' and empty all stored water containers?
items.prompt_hi: Swasthya vibhaag parivaaron se har hafte 'dry day' manaane aur saare jama paani ke bartan khaali karne ko kyon kehta hai?
items.answer: Mosquitoes lay eggs in still water, and the young take about a week to become adults; emptying containers weekly breaks the life cycle and reduces diseases like dengue and malaria.
hints: Ask how long egg to adult takes
Point to diseases mosquitoes spread
Prompt: once a ___ means none reach adulthood
Assert: weekly emptying breaks the cycle and cuts dengue

verified.solverAnswer: To remove standing water where mosquitoes breed; breaks the larva stage.

items.prompt_en: A farmer saves seeds from this year's best tomatoes to plant next year. Use the plant life cycle to explain why this works.
items.prompt_hi: Ek kisaan iss saal ke sabse achhe tamatar ke beej agle saal ke liye bacha ke rakhta hai. Paudhe ke jeevan-chakra se samjhao ye kyon kaam karta hai.
items.answer: The fruits contain seeds; next season the seeds germinate into seedlings, grow into plants, flower and make fruits again, so the cycle repeats.
hints: Ask what is inside a tomato
Point to the cycle starting again
Prompt: fruit gives ___, which grow into new ___
Assert: saved seeds restart the life cycle

verified.solverAnswer: Seeds carry the plant's traits, so they grow into plants like parents.

items.prompt_en: Draw the mosquito life cycle as a circle with four stages. Mark which stages live in water.
items.prompt_hi: Machhar ka jeevan-chakra chaar stages wale circle mein banao. Kaunse stages paani mein rehte hain, mark karo.
items.answer: Egg → larva → pupa → adult → back to egg. The eggs are laid on the water, the larva and pupa live in the water, and the adult flies in the air.
hints: Invite them to draw a water line on the page
Point to where the adult goes
Prompt: ___ and ___ live in water
Assert: eggs on water; larva and pupa in water; adult in air

verified.solverAnswer: Egg, larva, pupa in water; adult on air.

items.prompt_en: Golu's notebook says: 'Frog life cycle: egg → frog. Tadpoles are tiny fish.' Fix it.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ki notebook mein likha hai: 'Medhak ka jeevan-chakra: anda → medhak. Tadpole chhoti machhliyan hain.' Ise theek karo.
items.answer: Egg → tadpole → tadpole with legs → froglet → frog; tadpoles are young frogs, not fish.
hints: Ask what hatches from frog eggs
Point to the missing stages
Prompt: egg → ___ → froglet → frog
Assert: tadpoles are young frogs

verified.solverAnswer: Egg, tadpole, froglet, frog; tadpoles are baby frogs, not fish.

items.prompt_en: Explain to your neighbours how a mosquito grows and how they can stop mosquitoes breeding near their homes.
items.prompt_hi: Apne padosiyon ko samjhao ki machhar kaise badhta hai aur woh apne ghar ke paas machhar paidaa hone se kaise rok sakte hain.
items.answer: Key ideas: eggs are laid on still water → larvae → pupae (both in water) → adults in about a week; empty, scrub and cover water containers every week; don't let water collect in tyres, pots or coolers.
hints: Invite them to start with where eggs are laid
Point to the weekly timing
Prompt: egg, larva, ___, adult; empty water every ___
Assert: the stages plus a weekly 'dry day' plan

verified.solverAnswer: Eggs, larvae, pupae in stagnant water; adults; clear standing water, cover tanks.

items.prompt_en: From last time: what is the big change in a frog's body during its life cycle called?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: medhak ke jeevan-chakra mein shareer ke bade badlaav ko kya kehte hain?
items.answer: Metamorphosis.
hints: Ask how different a tadpole and a frog look
Point to the word for a big change in form
Prompt: this big change is called ___
Assert: metamorphosis

verified.solverAnswer: Metamorphosis.

workedExample.problem: Trace a frog's life cycle in a village pond during the monsoon.
steps: Frogs lay many eggs in a jelly (frogspawn) in the water
The eggs hatch into tadpoles with gills and a tail
The tadpoles grow back legs, then front legs
The tail shrinks and lungs form, making a froglet
The froglet becomes an adult frog that lives on land and in water and lays eggs again
fadedVersion: Frogs lay many ___ in a jelly in the water
The eggs hatch into ___ with gills and a tail
The tadpoles grow back legs, then ___ legs
The tail shrinks and ___ form, making a froglet
The froglet becomes an ___ frog that lays eggs again

skills.title: Say what a natural resource is and name the main ones
Describe the uses of air, water, sunlight, soil and forests
Show that air is a real resource: it takes up space and has weight

expectations: Natural resources are things in nature that people and other living things use: air, water, sunlight, soil, forests, minerals and fuels.
Air gives oxygen for breathing, carbon dioxide for plants to make food, and wind for drying, winnowing and wind energy; it is a resource even though it is free.
Water is needed for drinking, farming and cleaning, and by all living things; sunlight gives light and warmth, lets plants make food and gives solar energy.
Soil holds plants and gives them water and minerals; it takes hundreds of years to form and can be washed away quickly.
Forests give wood, fruits, leaves, honey and medicines, are home to many animals, hold the soil and help bring rain.
Air takes up space and has weight.

misconceptions.belief: Air is not a resource because it is free.
signs: Says only things we buy are resources
Shrugs at air pollution

diagnostic.prompt_en: Is air a natural resource?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kya hawa ek prakritik sansaadhan hai?

options.text: No, because nobody pays for it
Yes; we and all living things need it to breathe, plants use it, and wind is useful
Only when it is packed in cylinders

remediation.representation: 'What if it stopped?' card for air, water and sunlight
remediation.moveShape: Child imagines one minute without air, then lists who else depends on it; separate price from value

misconceptions.belief: Air is 'nothing': it has no weight and takes up no space.
signs: Calls an empty bottle 'khaali, kuch nahi'
Predicts the tissue in an upside-down glass will get wet

diagnostic.prompt_en: You push an empty glass straight down, upside down, into a bucket of water, with a dry tissue stuck at its bottom. What happens to the tissue?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek khaali glass ke tale mein sookha tissue chipka ke, glass ulta karke seedha baalti ke paani mein dabao. Tissue ka kya hoga?

options.text: It gets wet, because the glass is empty
It stays dry, because the air trapped in the glass takes up space and keeps the water out
The glass breaks

remediation.representation: Upside-down glass cross-section with a trapped air pocket
remediation.moveShape: Run the glass test; then tilt the glass so a bubble escapes and the tissue gets wet; child explains both

misconceptions.belief: Forests are useful only for wood.
signs: Lists only timber
Doesn't know how forest villages use the forest

diagnostic.prompt_en: What do forests give the people of villages in Odisha?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Odisha ke gaon ke logon ko jungle kya dete hain?

options.text: Only wood
Wood, fruits, sal leaves for plates, mahua flowers, honey, medicines, and clean air and water
Nothing; they are just trees

remediation.representation: Forest web diagram with village products around it
remediation.moveShape: Child adds one product per spoke and names who uses it

items.prompt_en: What is a natural resource? Name five.
items.prompt_hi: Prakritik sansaadhan kya hai? Paanch naam batao.
items.answer: Something from nature that living things use. Examples: air, water, sunlight, soil, forests (also minerals, coal, petroleum).
hints: Ask what we need from nature every day
Point to air and water first
Prompt: air, water, ___, soil and ___
Assert: things from nature we use; five examples

verified.solverAnswer: Anything from nature that we use: air, water, soil, sunlight, forests, minerals.

items.prompt_en: Give one use each of sunlight, soil and water.
items.prompt_hi: Dhoop, mitti aur paani ka ek-ek upyog batao.
items.answer: Sunlight: plants make food; drying clothes and grain; solar power; light and warmth. Soil: growing crops; making bricks and pots. Water: drinking, farming, cleaning.
hints: Ask what the farmer needs to grow wheat
Point to drying papad in the sun
Prompt: sunlight helps plants make ___
Assert: one sensible use for each

verified.solverAnswer: Sunlight: plants make food; soil: grow crops; water: drinking.

items.prompt_en: Predict: a dry tissue is stuck inside the bottom of an 'empty' glass. The glass is pushed straight down, upside down, into a bucket of water. Will the tissue get wet?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek 'khaali' glass ke tale mein sookha tissue chipka hai. Glass ko ulta karke seedha baalti ke paani mein dabaya. Kya tissue geela hoga?
items.answer: No, it stays dry; the air inside the glass takes up space and keeps the water out.
hints: Ask what is really inside the 'empty' glass
Point to air needing space
Prompt: the trapped air keeps the ___ out
Assert: it stays dry; air takes up space

verified.solverAnswer: No, stays dry (air in glass).

items.prompt_en: Predict: on a simple balance (a stick hung by a thread from its middle), you hang two identical balloons, one blown up and one empty. Which side goes down?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek saade taraazu pe (beech se dhaage pe latki lakdi), do ek jaise gubbare latkao, ek phula hua aur ek khaali. Kaunsi taraf jhukegi?
items.answer: The side with the blown-up balloon; the air pushed into it has weight.
hints: Ask what was added to one balloon
Point to the balance tipping
Prompt: the extra air has ___
Assert: the inflated side dips; air has weight

verified.solverAnswer: Blown-up balloon side goes down slightly (air has weight) though effect is tiny.
verified.note: Direction agrees (inflated side dips) but the effect is tiny on a stick-and-thread balance; with ordinary balloons the demo is often inconclusive. Use large balloons / a light metre-rule and a note that a small difference is expected.

items.prompt_en: Predict: a village cuts down all the forest on a hillside. What may happen to the soil there in the next monsoon?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek gaon pahaadi dhalaan ka poora jungle kaat deta hai. Agle monsoon mein wahan ki mitti ka kya ho sakta hai?
items.answer: Rain will wash the soil away (soil erosion), because there are no roots to hold it; landslides become more likely.
hints: Ask what tree roots do to soil
Point to heavy rain on a slope
Prompt: without roots, rain ___ the soil
Assert: soil erosion and landslide risk

verified.solverAnswer: Soil washed away (erosion), floods, landslides.

items.prompt_en: You said the tissue stays dry. Why couldn't the water get in?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne kaha tissue sookha rehta hai. Paani andar kyon nahi ja paaya?
items.answer: The glass was full of air; air takes up space, and with nowhere to escape it kept the water out.
hints: Ask what would happen if you tilted the glass
Point to the bubble escaping
Prompt: air filled the space, so water ___
Assert: trapped air occupies the space

verified.solverAnswer: Air in the glass takes up space and keeps water out.

items.prompt_en: Compare air and a bottle of packaged drinking water. You pay for one but not the other. Are both resources? Why?
items.prompt_hi: Hawa aur packed peene ke paani ki botal compare karo. Ek ke paise dete ho, doosre ke nahi. Kya dono sansaadhan hain? Kyon?
items.answer: Yes, both: a resource is anything useful from nature, whether we pay for it or not, and we can't live without air even for minutes.
hints: Ask which one we'd miss faster
Point to price versus need
Prompt: a resource is anything ___ from nature
Assert: both; price doesn't decide

verified.solverAnswer: Both; air free, bottled water costs because of treatment and packaging; both nature resources.

items.prompt_en: Name three things a farmer uses from nature to grow rice.
items.prompt_hi: Teen cheezein batao jo kisaan chawal ugane ke liye prakriti se leta hai.
items.answer: Any three: soil, water (rain, rivers, groundwater), sunlight, air (and seeds).
hints: Ask what a rice field is full of
Point to the sky over the field
Prompt: soil, water and ___
Assert: soil, water, sunlight, air

verified.solverAnswer: Soil, water, sunlight, air.

items.prompt_en: In many villages of Odisha and Jharkhand, families collect sal leaves, mahua flowers and kendu (tendu) leaves from forests. How do these help them, and why should forests be used carefully?
items.prompt_hi: Odisha aur Jharkhand ke kai gaon mein parivaar jungle se sal ke patte, mahua ke phool aur kendu (tendu) patte ikattha karte hain. Isse unki kya madad hoti hai, aur jungle ko soch-samajh ke kyon use karna chahiye?
items.answer: Sal leaves make plates and bring income; mahua flowers give food and oil; kendu leaves are sold for income; forests also give firewood and medicines. If people cut or take too much, the forest can't regrow, so they should take only what can grow back.
hints: Ask what each product is used for
Point to taking more than grows back
Prompt: forests give income and ___; overuse means they can't ___
Assert: many uses; take only what can regrow

verified.solverAnswer: They provide leaf plates, food, income; overuse destroys forests, so use sustainably.

items.prompt_en: Make a web diagram with 'Forest' in the middle and at least five arrows pointing to things it gives us.
items.prompt_hi: Ek web diagram banao, beech mein 'Jungle', aur kam se kam paanch teer un cheezon ki taraf jo woh hume deta hai.
items.answer: Any five: wood, fruits, honey, medicines, leaves, a home for animals, clean air, holding the soil, helping bring rain.
hints: Invite them to start with food from forests
Point to things we don't buy, like clean air
Prompt: wood, honey, ___, ___
Assert: at least five forest gifts

verified.solverAnswer: Forest: wood, fruits, medicines, honey, clean air, rain, animal homes.

items.prompt_en: Golu says: 'Air isn't a resource; it's free and everywhere, so it doesn't matter if factories make it dirty.' What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Hawa sansaadhan nahi hai; ye muft hai aur har jagah hai, isliye factory use ganda kare toh farak nahi padta.' Galti kya hai?
items.answer: Air is a vital resource; polluted air harms the breathing and health of people, animals and plants. Being free doesn't make it unimportant.
hints: Ask what happens to people's lungs in smoggy winters
Point to free versus important
Prompt: free doesn't mean ___
Assert: air is precious; pollution harms everyone

verified.solverAnswer: Air is a resource needed for life; dirty air harms health.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a younger child that air is 'something', not 'nothing', with one experiment.
items.prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko ek experiment ke saath samjhao ki hawa 'kuch' hai, 'kuch nahi' nahi.
items.answer: Key ideas: air takes up space (an upside-down glass keeps a tissue dry under water); air has weight (the balloon balance tips); we feel air as wind.
hints: Invite them to pick the glass or the balloon test
Point to what the result proves
Prompt: air takes up ___ and has ___
Assert: space and weight, shown by an experiment

verified.solverAnswer: Invert glass with tissue into water; tissue stays dry showing air occupies space.

items.prompt_en: From last time: why is soil called a precious resource?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: mitti ko keemti sansaadhan kyon kehte hain?
items.answer: Plants grow in it and get water and minerals from it; it takes hundreds of years to form but can be washed away quickly.
hints: Ask how long soil takes to form
Point to erosion on bare slopes
Prompt: soil takes ___ of years to form
Assert: slow to form, quick to lose, needed by plants

verified.solverAnswer: Soil takes ages to form, grows food, needed by plants; once eroded hard to replace.

Turn the glass upside down
Push it straight down into the water without tilting it
Lift it straight out and feel the tissue: it is dry

skills.title: Classify resources as renewable or non-renewable
Explain why some resources run out, and that renewable ones can also be overused
Suggest ways to use resources wisely

expectations: Renewable resources are replaced by nature in a short time: sunlight, wind, water through the water cycle, and forests if they are replanted.
Non-renewable resources are limited and take millions of years to form, so they can run out: coal, petroleum, natural gas and many minerals.
Even renewable resources can be overused: groundwater can be pumped out faster than rain refills it, and forests can be cut faster than they regrow.
Only a small part of Earth's water is fresh water we can use; most is salty sea water, and most fresh water is frozen as ice.
We can use resources wisely: save water, use solar and wind energy, use public transport, and reduce, reuse and recycle.

misconceptions.belief: Water can never run out because it rains every year.
signs: Leaves taps running
Says rain refills everything
Doesn't know wells and borewells can dry up

diagnostic.prompt_en: In some Indian cities, borewells have dried up even though it rains every year. Why?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Bharat ke kuch shehron mein har saal baarish hone ke baad bhi borewell sookh gaye. Kyon?

options.text: This can't happen; rain always refills the water
People pumped out groundwater faster than rain could refill it
The water evaporated from underground pipes

remediation.representation: Groundwater tank diagram: rain inflow tap vs borewell outflow tap
remediation.moveShape: Child sets inflow and outflow on the diagram and watches the level fall when outflow wins

misconceptions.belief: Renewable means unlimited, so we can use as much as we like.
signs: Says forests are renewable so cutting is fine
Ignores how long trees take to grow

diagnostic.prompt_en: Forests are renewable. Does that mean we can cut as many trees as we like?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Jungle renewable hain. Kya iska matlab hai jitne chahe utne ped kaat sakte hain?

options.text: Yes, renewable means it never runs out
No; trees take many years to grow, so if we cut faster than they regrow, the forest is lost
Yes, if we cut them in winter

remediation.representation: Cut-rate vs regrow-rate timeline over 30 years
remediation.moveShape: Child plays both rates on the timeline and finds the cutting rate that keeps the forest

misconceptions.belief: Petrol and coal can be made from scratch whenever we need them, so they will never run out.
signs: Thinks petrol pumps 'make' petrol
Says factories can make more coal

diagnostic.prompt_en: Where does petrol come from?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Petrol kahan se aata hai?

options.text: It is made from scratch in factories using air and water, so it can never run out
It is refined from petroleum (crude oil), which formed underground from the remains of tiny living things over millions of years
From sea water

remediation.representation: Deep-time strip: tiny sea organisms → buried → millions of years → crude oil → refinery → petrol
remediation.moveShape: Child places today's use on the strip and compares a lifetime with millions of years

items.prompt_en: Sort into renewable and non-renewable: sunlight, coal, wind, petroleum, water, natural gas.
items.prompt_hi: Renewable aur non-renewable mein baanto: dhoop, koyla, hawa, petroleum, paani, prakritik gas.
items.answer: Renewable: sunlight, wind, water. Non-renewable: coal, petroleum, natural gas.
hints: Ask which ones come back every day
Point to fuels dug from underground
Prompt: sun, wind and ___ are renewable
Assert: sun, wind, water renewable; coal, petroleum, gas not

verified.solverAnswer: Renewable: sunlight, wind, water (via water cycle, if used carefully). Non-renewable: coal, petroleum, natural gas.

items.prompt_en: Why is coal called non-renewable?
items.prompt_hi: Koyle ko non-renewable kyon kehte hain?
items.answer: It took millions of years to form from buried plants, and we use it far faster than it can form, so it will run out.
hints: Ask how coal was made
Point to the time it took
Prompt: it took ___ of years to form
Assert: formed over millions of years; used far faster

verified.solverAnswer: Takes millions of years to form; used faster than formed, will run out.

items.prompt_en: Predict: a town pumps out lots of groundwater every day for years, more than the rain soaks back into the ground. What happens to the water level in its wells?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek shehar saalon tak roz bahut zameen ka paani nikaalta hai, jitna baarish wapas zameen mein jaati hai usse zyada. Uske kuon mein paani ke star ka kya hoga?
items.answer: It keeps falling, and wells and borewells may dry up.
hints: Ask what happens to a bucket if you take out more than you pour in
Point to rain refilling slowly
Prompt: taking out more than goes in makes the level ___
Assert: the water level falls; wells can dry up

verified.solverAnswer: The water level falls; wells go dry.

items.prompt_en: Predict: one car runs on petrol and another is an electric car charged with solar panels. After ten years of running, which one has been using up a non-renewable resource?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek car petrol se chalti hai aur doosri electric car solar panel se charge hoti hai. Das saal chalne ke baad, kaunsi car non-renewable sansaadhan khatam kar rahi thi?
items.answer: The petrol car, because petroleum is non-renewable; the solar-charged car runs on renewable sunlight.
hints: Ask where each car's energy comes from
Point to sunlight returning daily
Prompt: petrol comes from ___, which runs out
Assert: the petrol car uses up a non-renewable resource

verified.solverAnswer: The petrol car.

items.prompt_en: You said wells can dry up even though it rains. Why doesn't the rain keep them full?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne kaha baarish ke baad bhi kuen sookh sakte hain. Baarish unhe bhara kyon nahi rakhti?
items.answer: Rain refills groundwater only slowly and partly (much of it runs off, especially from concrete); if we pump faster than it refills, the level falls.
hints: Ask where rain goes on a concrete road
Point to inflow versus outflow
Prompt: we pump ___ than rain refills
Assert: slow refill plus fast pumping lowers the level

verified.solverAnswer: People pump out groundwater faster than rain refills it; also concrete surfaces block seepage.

items.prompt_en: Compare sunlight and petrol as sources of energy.
items.prompt_hi: Urja ke source ke roop mein dhoop aur petrol compare karo.
items.answer: Sunlight is renewable, free, clean and comes back every day; petrol is non-renewable, limited and pollutes the air when burned.
hints: Ask which one will still be here in a million years
Point to smoke from vehicles
Prompt: sunlight is ___ and clean; petrol is ___ and polluting
Assert: renewable and clean vs limited and polluting

verified.solverAnswer: Sunlight: renewable, doesn't run out, clean; petrol: non-renewable, limited, pollutes.

items.prompt_en: Give three ways your family can save water at home.
items.prompt_hi: Teen tareeke batao jinse tumhara parivaar ghar pe paani bacha sakta hai.
items.answer: Any three: turn off the tap while brushing; take a bucket bath instead of a long shower; fix leaking taps; reuse water from washing vegetables or RO waste water for plants or cleaning; collect rainwater.
hints: Ask how much water runs while brushing
Point to leaking taps
Prompt: close the tap, use a ___, fix ___
Assert: three practical water-saving habits

verified.solverAnswer: Turn off taps, fix leaks, reuse RO/vegetable-wash water, bucket bath, harvest rain.

items.prompt_en: There is so much water on Earth. Why can't we just use sea water for our homes and farms?
items.prompt_hi: Dharti pe itna paani hai. Hum ghar aur kheton ke liye samundar ka paani hi kyon nahi use kar sakte?
items.answer: About 97% of Earth's water is salty sea water, which is unfit for drinking and for most crops, and removing the salt takes a lot of energy; of the small amount of fresh water, most is frozen, so very little is easy to use.
hints: Ask what sea water tastes like
Point to how little is fresh
Prompt: about ___% of Earth's water is salty
Assert: mostly salty; little usable fresh water

verified.solverAnswer: Sea water is salty; unfit to drink or irrigate; removing salt is costly.

items.prompt_en: Imagine all of Earth's water filled a bucket of 100 mugs. Draw it and show about how many mugs are fresh water, and how many of those are frozen.
items.prompt_hi: Socho Dharti ka saara paani 100 mug wali ek baalti mein hai. Drawing banao aur dikhao ki lagbhag kitne mug meetha paani hai, aur unme se kitne jame hue hain.
items.answer: About 3 mugs are fresh water, and about 2 of those are frozen as ice; the remaining roughly 1 mug is mostly underground, with only a tiny bit in rivers and lakes.
hints: Invite them to shade the salty part first
Point to ice in glaciers and at the poles
Prompt: about ___ fresh, of which about ___ frozen
Assert: ~97 salty, ~3 fresh, ~2 of those frozen

verified.solverAnswer: Around 97 salt, 3 fresh, of which about 2 frozen (about 1 usable).

items.prompt_en: Golu says: 'Trees are renewable, so we can cut down the whole forest; it will grow back next year.' What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Ped renewable hain, isliye poora jungle kaat sakte hain; agle saal wapas ug jaayega.' Galti kya hai?
items.answer: Trees take many years, even decades, to grow; cutting faster than they regrow destroys the forest and the animals' homes. A forest stays renewable only if it is used carefully and replanted.
hints: Ask how old a big neem tree is
Point to 'next year'
Prompt: a tree takes ___ to grow
Assert: renewable isn't unlimited

verified.solverAnswer: Forests take decades to regrow; cutting faster than regrowth destroys it.

items.prompt_en: Explain to your family the difference between renewable and non-renewable resources, and two habits that help.
items.prompt_hi: Apne parivaar ko renewable aur non-renewable sansaadhanon ka farak samjhao, aur do aadatein jo madad karti hain.
items.answer: Key ideas: renewable resources are replaced by nature quickly (sun, wind, water) but can still be overused; non-renewable ones formed over millions of years and are limited (coal, petrol, gas); habits: switch off lights and fans, walk, cycle or use public transport, save water, use solar power.
hints: Invite them to give one example of each kind
Point to overuse of renewables too
Prompt: renewable comes back ___; non-renewable took ___ of years
Assert: the difference plus two wise-use habits

verified.solverAnswer: Renewable are replaced naturally (sunlight, wind); non-renewable run out (coal, petrol). Habits: save electricity/fuel, walk, save water.

items.prompt_en: From last time: name one renewable and one non-renewable source of energy.
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: urja ka ek renewable aur ek non-renewable source batao.
items.answer: Renewable: sunlight, wind or flowing water. Non-renewable: coal, petroleum or natural gas.
hints: Ask what powers a solar panel
Point to the petrol pump
Prompt: renewable ___; non-renewable ___
Assert: e.g. sunlight and coal

verified.solverAnswer: Renewable: sunlight/wind; non-renewable: coal/petrol.

workedExample.problem: Classify petrol and decide how to use it wisely.
steps: Ask how it is formed: refined from crude oil that formed underground over millions of years
Ask whether nature can replace it quickly: no
So it is non-renewable
Effects of overuse: it will run out, and burning it pollutes the air
Wise use: share rides, use public transport, cycle, and switch to solar or electric where possible
