skills.title: Explain what stars are and why they look tiny
Identify constellations such as Saptarishi and Orion, and use the pointer stars to find the Pole Star (Dhruva tara)
Explain why stars seem to move across the night sky and why the Pole Star seems fixed

expectations: Stars are huge, very hot balls of glowing gas that make their own light; the Sun is a star, the one nearest to us.
Other stars look like tiny dots because they are extremely far away.
Stars are in the sky during the day too, but sunlight scattered by the air makes the sky too bright to see them.
A constellation is a group of stars that forms a pattern as seen from Earth, e.g. Saptarishi (part of Ursa Major, the Big Dipper) and Orion (called Mriga in some Indian traditions).
The two pointer stars of Saptarishi point towards the Pole Star (Dhruva tara), which shows the direction north; the Pole Star is not the brightest star in the sky.
Stars seem to move from east to west across the night sky because the Earth spins from west to east; the Pole Star seems almost fixed because it lies nearly in line with the Earth's axis.
A 'shooting star' is not a star but a small piece of rock or dust from space burning up in our air.

misconceptions.belief: Stars are tiny and close to the Earth.
signs: Thinks stars are small lights just above the clouds
Thinks an aeroplane could reach a star

diagnostic.prompt_en: Why do stars look like tiny dots?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Taare chhote-chhote bindu jaise kyon dikhte hain?

options.text: Because they really are small, like light bulbs
Because they are huge but extremely far away
Because they are behind clouds

They are still in the sky, but the bright sunlit sky hides them
They go below the ground

remediation.moveShape: Shine a torch in a bright room and a dark room; child explains why the same torch seems to vanish

misconceptions.belief: The Pole Star is the brightest star in the sky.
signs: Looks for the brightest star to find north
Calls any bright star 'Dhruva tara'

diagnostic.prompt_en: How can you find the Pole Star?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Dhruva tara kaise dhundhenge?

options.text: Find the brightest star in the sky
Follow the two pointer stars of Saptarishi; the Pole Star is a not-very-bright star in line with them
It is always straight overhead

remediation.moveShape: Child traces the pointer line on the map, then compares Polaris's brightness with Sirius

misconceptions.belief: A shooting star is a real star falling to Earth.
signs: Says 'a star fell from the sky'
Thinks stars can drop down

diagnostic.prompt_en: What is a 'shooting star'?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: 'Toota taara' (shooting star) asal mein kya hai?

options.text: A star falling down to Earth
A small piece of rock or dust from space burning up in our air
The light of an aeroplane

remediation.representation: Scale picture: a huge distant star vs a pebble-sized meteor glowing high in the air
remediation.moveShape: Ask how a star many times bigger than Earth could fall onto it; then show the meteor's real size

items.prompt_en: What is a star? Name the star nearest to Earth.
items.prompt_hi: Taara kya hota hai? Dharti ke sabse paas wala taara kaunsa hai?
items.answer: A huge ball of very hot, glowing gas that gives out its own light. The Sun is the nearest star.
hints: Ask where the Sun's light comes from
Point to the Sun as a star
Prompt: a star is a huge ball of ___ gas
Assert: a glowing gas ball; the Sun is the nearest

verified.solverAnswer: A huge ball of hot glowing gas that makes its own light; nearest star is the Sun.

items.prompt_en: What is a constellation? Name two.
items.prompt_hi: Taaramandal (constellation) kya hota hai? Do naam batao.
items.answer: A group of stars that forms a pattern as seen from Earth. Examples: Saptarishi (Ursa Major or Big Dipper), Orion (Mriga), Cassiopeia, Leo.
hints: Ask what shape Saptarishi makes
Point to joining stars into a picture
Prompt: a star pattern is a ___
Assert: a star pattern; e.g. Saptarishi and Orion

verified.solverAnswer: A group of stars forming a pattern: Saptarishi (Ursa Major), Orion.

items.prompt_en: Predict: how does a big street lamp look from 5 km away at night, compared with from 50 metres? What does this tell you about stars?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: raat mein ek badi street light 5 km door se kaisi dikhegi, 50 metre ke mukaable? Isse taaron ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai?
items.answer: From far away it looks like a tiny point of light; stars look tiny because they are very far away, even though they are huge.
hints: Ask how a train's headlight looks from very far
Point to distance shrinking things
Prompt: farther things look ___
Assert: tiny because far, not because small

verified.solverAnswer: Looks like a tiny dot from far; stars look tiny because they're very far.

items.prompt_en: Predict: on a winter night at 8 pm you see Orion low in the eastern sky. Where will it be around midnight?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: sardi ki raat 8 baje tumhe Orion poorab ke aasmaan mein neeche dikhta hai. Aadhi raat ke aaspaas woh kahan hoga?
items.answer: Higher up in the sky, having moved westward; stars rise in the east and set in the west, like the Sun.
hints: Ask where the Sun goes after rising in the east
Point to the Earth spinning
Prompt: stars move from ___ to ___
Assert: it climbs higher and moves westward

verified.solverAnswer: High in the south (moved up/westward through the night).

items.prompt_en: Predict: you point a camera at the northern sky from a rooftop and take a photo that stays open for several hours. What pattern will the stars make, and which star stays almost still?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: chhat se camera ko uttar ke aasmaan ki taraf rakh ke kai ghanton ki ek photo li. Taare kaisa pattern banayenge, aur kaunsa taara lagbhag wahin rahega?
items.answer: The stars draw circular trails (arcs) around one point; the Pole Star stays almost at the centre.
hints: Ask what the Earth is doing all night
Point to the axis pointing near the Pole Star
Prompt: stars draw ___ around the ___
Assert: circular trails around the nearly still Pole Star

verified.solverAnswer: Circular arcs (trails) around the Pole Star; Pole Star stays almost still.
verified.note: Science agrees. SAFETY advisory: rooftop at night; add 'with an adult, away from the edge' or use a window/courtyard.

items.prompt_en: You found the Pole Star using the pointer stars. Why does the Pole Star help travellers find north?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne pointer taaron se Dhruva tara dhundha. Dhruva tara yatriyon ko north dhundhne mein kyon madad karta hai?
items.answer: It lies almost straight above the Earth's North Pole, nearly in line with the Earth's axis, so it stays nearly fixed in the northern sky while other stars move.
hints: Ask what the camera photo showed
Point to the Earth's axis
Prompt: it lies almost above the Earth's ___
Assert: it stays nearly fixed in the north

verified.solverAnswer: It lies almost exactly above Earth's north axis, so it always shows north.

items.prompt_en: Compare the Sun with a star you see at night. How are they alike, and why do they look so different?
items.prompt_hi: Suraj aur raat mein dikhne wale kisi taare ko compare karo. Dono ek jaise kaise hain, aur itne alag kyon dikhte hain?
items.answer: Both are stars, hot glowing balls of gas. The Sun is much nearer, so it looks big and bright; the other stars are much farther away and look like dots.
hints: Ask what both are made of
Point to distance
Prompt: the Sun looks big because it is ___
Assert: same kind of object; distance changes how it looks

verified.solverAnswer: Sun is a star; alike: hot glowing gas, own light; Sun is much nearer so looks big and bright.

items.prompt_en: Why can't we see stars on a clear, sunny afternoon, but can see them at night from the same place?
items.prompt_hi: Saaf dhoop wali dopahar mein taare kyon nahi dikhte, jabki usi jagah se raat mein dikh jaate hain?
items.answer: The stars are there all day, but sunlight scattered by the air makes the sky so bright that their faint light is hidden; at night the sky is dark.
hints: Ask what the torch did in the bright room
Point to the bright daytime sky
Prompt: the stars are there, but the sky is too ___
Assert: daylight hides them; they don't switch off

verified.solverAnswer: Sunlight scatters in sky and its brightness hides faint stars; stars are still there.

items.prompt_en: Long ago, sailors and camel caravans crossing the Thar desert at night used the stars. How could they keep heading north?
items.prompt_hi: Bahut pehle naavik aur Thar registaan paar karte oont ke kaafile raat mein taaron ka sahara lete the. Woh north ki taraf kaise chalte rehte the?
items.answer: They found the Pole Star (using Saptarishi's pointer stars) and travelled towards it, because it stays fixed in the north.
hints: Ask which star doesn't move across the sky
Point to the pointer stars
Prompt: walk towards the ___
Assert: follow the Pole Star north

verified.solverAnswer: Find the Pole Star using Saptarishi and keep it ahead.

items.prompt_en: Draw the seven stars of Saptarishi as dots joined by lines. Mark the two pointer stars and draw an arrow from them to the Pole Star.
items.prompt_hi: Saptarishi ke saat taaron ko bindu bana ke lakeeron se jodo. Do pointer taare mark karo aur unse Dhruva tare tak teer banao.
items.answer: A ladle (or question-mark) shape; the two pointer stars are at the outer edge of the bowl, far from the handle; the arrow runs from them to the Pole Star, about five times the gap between them.
acceptable: two stars at the edge of the bowl
hints: Invite them to draw the bowl and the handle
Point to the bowl's outer edge
Prompt: the pointers are at the edge of the ___
Assert: ladle shape; pointers on the bowl point to the Pole Star

verified.solverAnswer: Seven dots forming a ladle shape, two end stars point to Pole Star.

items.prompt_en: Golu says: 'I saw a star fall from the sky last night! Shooting stars are stars dropping down.' What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Kal raat maine ek taara aasmaan se girte dekha! Toote taare asli taare hote hain jo neeche girte hain.' Galti kya hai?
items.answer: A shooting star is a meteor: a small piece of rock or dust from space burning up in Earth's air. Real stars are huge and very far away and don't fall.
hints: Ask how big a real star is compared with Earth
Point to the streak being in our air
Prompt: a shooting star is a small ___ burning up
Assert: a meteor, not a star

verified.solverAnswer: Shooting star is a meteor, space rock burning in the atmosphere, not a star.

items.prompt_en: Explain to your younger sister why stars seem to move across the night sky, and why one star, Dhruva tara, seems to stay in place.
items.prompt_hi: Apni chhoti behen ko samjhao ki taare raat ke aasmaan mein chalte hue kyon lagte hain, aur ek taara, Dhruva tara, ek jagah tika hua kyon lagta hai.
items.answer: Key ideas: the Earth spins from west to east, so stars appear to move from east to west; the Pole Star is almost in line with the Earth's axis, so it seems fixed; the stars themselves are not moving across our sky like that.
hints: Invite them to spin on the spot and watch the room
Point to the axis line
Prompt: the ___ spins, so stars seem to move; Dhruva tara is on the ___
Assert: Earth's spin explains it; the Pole Star is near the axis

verified.solverAnswer: Earth rotates making stars appear to move east to west; the Pole Star lies above Earth's axis so stays put.

items.prompt_en: From last time: which group of stars helps us find the Pole Star?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: kaunsa taaramandal Dhruva tara dhundhne mein madad karta hai?
items.answer: Saptarishi (Ursa Major or Big Dipper), using its two pointer stars.
hints: Ask about the ladle-shaped group
Point to the pointer stars
Prompt: the ___ points to Dhruva tara
Assert: Saptarishi

verified.solverAnswer: Saptarishi (Ursa Major/Big Dipper).

workedExample.problem: Find north at night using Saptarishi.
steps: With an adult, go to a dark rooftop and face the northern part of the sky
Find seven bright stars making a big ladle or question-mark shape
Pick the two stars at the outer edge of the ladle's bowl: the pointer stars
Follow the line through them for about five times the gap between them
The moderately bright star there is the Pole Star; the direction below it is north

skills.title: Name the eight planets in order from the Sun
Compare the sizes and distances of the Sun and planets
Explain that the Moon and planets shine by reflected sunlight, and planets usually don't twinkle
Explain that seasons are not caused by Earth's distance from the Sun

expectations: The solar system is the Sun and everything that goes around it: eight planets, their moons, dwarf planets, asteroids and comets.
In order from the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
Jupiter is the largest planet and Mercury the smallest; the Sun is far bigger than all of them (more than 100 Earths would fit across it).
Planets and the Moon do not make their own light; they shine by reflecting sunlight. Stars twinkle; planets usually shine steadily.
Venus is the brightest planet, often seen as the 'morning star' or 'evening star', but it is a planet, not a star; it is the hottest planet because its thick atmosphere traps heat.
Seasons are caused by the tilt of the Earth's axis, not by its distance from the Sun; the Earth is actually closest to the Sun in early January.
Never look directly at the Sun.

misconceptions.belief: The Moon gives off its own light.
signs: Says the Moon 'glows' like a bulb
Can't explain the Moon's phases

It reflects sunlight that falls on it
It reflects the light of cities on Earth

remediation.moveShape: Child watches both and names the difference, then labels which one makes its own light

misconceptions.belief: Seasons happen because the Earth is nearer the Sun in summer.

Links heat only to distance

diagnostic.prompt_en: The Earth is closest to the Sun in early January. What season is it in India then?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Dharti January ki shuruaat mein Suraj ke sabse paas hoti hai. Tab Bharat mein kaunsa mausam hota hai?

Monsoon

items.prompt_en: Name the eight planets in order, starting from the one nearest the Sun.

Budh Shukra Prithvi Mangal Brihaspati Shani Arun Varun

Point to the memory sentence

Assert: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune

verified.solverAnswer: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

items.prompt_en: Which is the largest planet, and which is the smallest?
items.prompt_hi: Sabse bada grah kaunsa hai aur sabse chhota kaunsa?
items.answer: Largest: Jupiter. Smallest: Mercury.
hints: Ask about the giant planet with the big red spot
Point to the one nearest the Sun
Prompt: largest ___, smallest ___
Assert: Jupiter largest, Mercury smallest

verified.solverAnswer: Largest Jupiter; smallest Mercury.

items.prompt_en: Make up your own sentence where each word starts with the first letter of a planet, in order: M, V, E, M, J, S, U, N.
items.prompt_hi: Apna ek vaakya banao jiska har shabd grahon ke pehle akshar se, kram se, shuru ho: M, V, E, M, J, S, U, N.

acceptable: My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Noodles
hints: Invite them to say the letters aloud first
Point to one word per planet
Assert: any sentence with initials M V E M J S U N

verified.solverAnswer: Any mnemonic e.g. My Very Easy Method Just Speeds Up Navigation.

items.prompt_en: Predict: on a clear evening you see Venus and a bright star near it. Which one twinkles more?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: saaf shaam mein tumhe Shukra (Venus) aur uske paas ek chamakdaar taara dikhta hai. Kaun zyada timtimaayega?
items.answer: The star twinkles; Venus shines steadily, as planets usually do.
hints: Ask which one makes its own light
Point to planets shining steadily
Prompt: stars ___; planets usually shine ___
Assert: the star twinkles; Venus is steady

verified.solverAnswer: The star twinkles; Venus (planet) shines steadily.

items.prompt_en: Predict: Mercury is nearest the Sun and Venus is second. Which planet is the hottest?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: Budh (Mercury) Suraj ke sabse paas hai aur Shukra (Venus) doosre number pe. Sabse garam grah kaunsa hai?
items.answer: Venus; its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, making it hotter than Mercury.
hints: Ask what a blanket does to warmth
Point to Venus's thick atmosphere
Prompt: a thick atmosphere ___ heat
Assert: Venus is hottest; its atmosphere traps heat

verified.solverAnswer: Venus (thick atmosphere traps heat).

items.prompt_en: Predict: in early January the Earth is at its closest to the Sun all year. Is it summer or winter in India then?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: January ki shuruaat mein Dharti poore saal mein Suraj ke sabse paas hoti hai. Tab Bharat mein garmi hoti hai ya sardi?
items.answer: Winter; so distance doesn't cause the seasons; the tilt of the Earth's axis does.
hints: Ask what the weather is like in January
Point to the closest distance happening then
Prompt: closest to the Sun, yet it's ___
Assert: winter; tilt, not distance, causes seasons

verified.solverAnswer: Winter; distance doesn't cause seasons.

items.prompt_en: You said the Moon reflects sunlight. Why then do we see the Moon change shape (phases) during a month?
items.prompt_hi: Tumne kaha chaand Suraj ki roshni reflect karta hai. Toh mahine bhar mein chaand ka aakaar (kalaayein) kyon badalta dikhta hai?
items.answer: The Moon goes around the Earth, so from Earth we see different amounts of its sunlit half, which makes its shape seem to change.
hints: Ask which half of the Moon is always lit
Point to the ball-and-lamp model
Prompt: we see different amounts of its ___ half
Assert: phases come from viewing angle, not the Moon's own light

verified.solverAnswer: We see different amounts of its sunlit half as it orbits Earth.

items.prompt_en: Compare Earth and Jupiter: which is bigger, which is closer to the Sun, and what is each mostly made of?
items.prompt_hi: Dharti aur Brihaspati compare karo: kaun bada hai, kaun Suraj ke paas hai, aur dono zyada-tar kis cheez se bane hain?
items.answer: Jupiter is much bigger (about 11 Earths across); Earth is closer to the Sun; Earth is rocky while Jupiter is mostly gas.
hints: Ask where each comes in the planet order
Point to rocky inner and gassy outer planets
Prompt: Jupiter is ___; Earth is ___
Assert: Jupiter bigger and gassy; Earth closer and rocky

verified.solverAnswer: Jupiter is bigger; Earth is closer to the Sun; Earth is rocky, Jupiter is mostly gas (hydrogen, helium).

items.prompt_en: Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander and Pragyan rover ran on solar panels. Why did they have to stop working when night came on the Moon?
items.prompt_hi: Chandrayaan-3 ke Vikram lander aur Pragyan rover solar panel se chalte the. Chaand pe raat aane pe unhe kaam kyon rokna pada?
items.answer: They needed sunlight for power; the Moon makes no light of its own, so during the long lunar night (about 14 Earth days) there was no sunlight, and it also becomes extremely cold.
hints: Ask what powers a solar panel
Point to the Moon not glowing by itself
Prompt: at lunar night there is no ___
Assert: no sunlight, no power; the Moon has no light of its own

verified.solverAnswer: No sunlight at night on Moon so no solar power, and extreme cold.

items.prompt_en: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth. If the Sun suddenly went dark, how long would it be before we noticed?
items.prompt_hi: Suraj ki roshni ko Dharti tak pahunchne mein lagbhag 8 minute lagte hain. Agar Suraj achaanak bujh jaaye, toh humein kitni der baad pata chalega?
items.answer: About 8 minutes, because the light already on its way would keep arriving until then.
hints: Ask how long sunlight takes to reach us
Point to light already travelling
Prompt: we'd keep seeing light for about ___
Assert: about 8 minutes

verified.solverAnswer: About 8 minutes.

items.prompt_en: Draw the Sun and the eight planets in order along a line. Make Jupiter the biggest circle and Mercury the smallest. Which planet comes right after Earth?
items.prompt_hi: Suraj aur aathon grahon ko kram se ek line pe banao. Brihaspati sabse bada gola aur Budh sabse chhota. Dharti ke theek baad kaunsa grah aata hai?
items.answer: Mars.
hints: Invite them to place the Sun at one end
Point to the fourth planet
Prompt: Earth, then ___
Assert: Mars comes after Earth

verified.solverAnswer: Mars.

items.prompt_en: Golu says: 'It's hot in May because the Earth goes nearest to the Sun in May.' What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Mai mein garmi isliye hoti hai kyonki Mai mein Dharti Suraj ke sabse paas jaati hai.' Galti kya hai?
items.answer: Seasons are caused by the tilt of the Earth's axis: in May the Sun's rays fall more directly on India and the days are longer. The Earth is actually closest to the Sun in January.
hints: Ask when the Earth is actually closest to the Sun
Point to sunlight angle and day length
Prompt: seasons come from the Earth's ___
Assert: tilt, not distance; closest is in January

verified.solverAnswer: Seasons are due to Earth's tilt, not distance; Earth is nearest in January.

items.prompt_en: Explain to your friend the difference between a star and a planet, using the Sun, the Moon and Venus.
items.prompt_hi: Apne dost ko Suraj, Chaand aur Shukra ke example se taare aur grah ka farak samjhao.
items.answer: Key ideas: a star like the Sun makes its own light and is a huge ball of hot glowing gas; planets like Venus and moons like our Moon don't make light but reflect sunlight; planets go around the Sun and the Moon goes around the Earth; stars twinkle, planets usually don't.
hints: Invite them to sort the three into 'makes light' and 'reflects light'
Point to what goes around what

skills.title: Describe the Milky Way as our galaxy of billions of stars, seen as a faint band in dark skies
Order Earth, the Sun, the solar system, the Milky Way and the universe by size

expectations: A galaxy is a huge collection of billions of stars, together with gas and dust.
Our solar system is inside the Milky Way galaxy; on very dark nights it is seen as a faint, milky band of light across the sky.
The Sun is one ordinary, medium-sized star in the Milky Way, far from its centre; it looks biggest and brightest to us only because it is the nearest star.
Many stars are far bigger than the Sun; Betelgeuse in Orion is hundreds of times wider.
The universe contains billions of galaxies; distances are so huge that they are measured in light-years, the distance light travels in one year.
City lights hide the Milky Way; dark-sky places like Hanle in Ladakh are protected so the sky can be studied.

workedExample.problem: Explain why the Sun looks bigger than Betelgeuse even though Betelgeuse is much bigger.
steps: Compare sizes: Betelgeuse is hundreds of times wider than the Sun
Compare distances: the Sun is about 150 million km away; Betelgeuse is hundreds of light-years away
Rule: the farther away something is, the smaller it looks
So the huge, distant star looks like a dot and the nearby, medium-sized star looks big
Conclusion: how big a star looks depends on its distance, not only its real size
